2e96fa723c02984165b8e3b997e69e0510605832.title: Uniform cubic mean-square bound
2e96fa723c02984165b8e3b997e69e0510605832.body:
Let \(c_f\) and \(C_f\) be the lower and upper density envelopes, and let \(L\) be the common Hölder radius. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Envelope constants.)} \(0<c_f<1\), \(1<C_f\), and \(1<L\).
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} The common source and target sample size \(n\) satisfies
\[
n\ge n_0=256.
\]
\item \textbf{(Model.)} \(P\in\mathcal M_n\), with \(\mathcal M_n\) defined in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\end{itemize}
For each \(A\in\{Y,D\}\), let \(\widehat T_A\) be the statistic in \cref{obj:def:cubic-estimator}, and let \(T_A\) be the target-averaged source contrast,
\[
T_A
=
\int_{\text{covariate space}}
f_{\mathrm T}(x)\bigl(m_{A1}(x)-m_{A0}(x)\bigr)\,dx.
\]
Then, under the equal-size source–target sampling law specified by \(P\),
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[(\widehat T_A-T_A)^2\right]
\le C_{\mathrm{mse}}\,n^{-2/3},
\]
where the finite, explicitly computable constant \(C_{\mathrm{mse}}=C_{\mathrm{mse}}(c_f,C_f,L)\) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_{\mathrm{mse}}
={}&3\Bigg\{
\left[2(1+C_f)^2(4/c_f)^5\right]^2 7^8
\Big[
2^7\,8!\,
\big\{(1+C_f+C_f^2)^4 5^{4/5}
 +(1+C_f+C_f^2)5^{7/5}\big\}\\
&\hspace{48mm}
+2^8[3(1+C_f)L]^8 5^{4/5}
\Big]\\
&\quad
+7^4[48(1+C_f)^2(4/c_f)^5]^2
 [3(1+C_f)L]^4 2^{1/2}5^{2/3}\\
&\quad
+2\Big[
\big\{24(1+C_f)^2(4/c_f)^5
       7^2[3(1+C_f)L]^2\big\}^2
 7^2\\
&\hspace{24mm}\cdot
\big\{2(1+C_f+C_f^2)5^{1/5}
 +2^{5/4}[3(1+C_f)L]^2 5^{1/5}\big\}
 2^{1/2}5^{1/2}\\
&\hspace{16mm}
+\big\{8(1+C_f)^2(4/c_f)^5
       7^3[3(1+C_f)L]^3\big\}^2
 2^{3/4}5^{3/4}
\Big]
\Bigg\}\\
&+3\Bigg\{
10\cdot7^2[48(1+C_f)^2(4/c_f)^5]^2\\
&\quad
+60\cdot7^4(2^2-1)^2
 [48(1+C_f)^2(4/c_f)^5]^2
 [1+2(1+C_f)]^4[2+C_f+C_f^2]^2\\
&\quad
+310\cdot7^6(2^3-1)^2
 [48(1+C_f)^2(4/c_f)^5]^2
 [1+2(1+C_f)]^6[2+C_f+C_f^2]^3
\Bigg\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

e1d6d765787f36ca7704e2d53ffb8132f8fde09e.title: Transported complier effect identification
e1d6d765787f36ca7704e2d53ffb8132f8fde09e.body:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) and let \(P\) be a transport law satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Lower envelope.)} \(0<c_f<1\), where \(c_f\) is the lower density envelope.
\item \textbf{(Upper envelope.)} \(1<C_f\), where \(C_f\) is the upper density envelope.
\item \textbf{(Smoothness radius.)} \(1<L\), where \(L\) is the common Hölder radius.
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\in\mathcal M_n\), the model class of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with constants \(c_f,C_f,L\).
\end{itemize}
Write \(P_n^F\) for the full-data law, \(D(z)\) for potential receipt under encouragement \(z\), and \(Y(d)\) for potential outcome under receipt \(d\). For each \(z\in\{0,1\}\), there are versions of the source conditional means such that, almost everywhere under the source covariate law,
\[
m_{Dz}(x)
 =\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[D(z)\mid X=x,S=1],
\qquad
m_{Yz}(x)
 =\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[Y(D(z))\mid X=x,S=1].
\]
Here \(m_{Dz}\) and \(m_{Yz}\) are the source receipt and outcome arm means.

Define the source arm contrasts and the complier indicator by
\[
\Delta_D(x)=m_{D1}(x)-m_{D0}(x),
\qquad
\Delta_Y(x)=m_{Y1}(x)-m_{Y0}(x),
\qquad
C=\mathbf 1\{D(1)=1,\ D(0)=0\}.
\]
There are common versions of the conditional means in each of the following chains for which, for \(P_{\mathrm T}\)-almost every \(x\), where \(P_{\mathrm T}\) is the target covariate law,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta_D(x)
&=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[D(1)-D(0)\mid X=x,S=1]\\
&=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[C\mid X=x,S=1]
 =\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[C\mid X=x,S=0],\\
\Delta_Y(x)
&=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[Y(D(1))-Y(D(0))\mid X=x,S=1]\\
&=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[(Y(1)-Y(0))C\mid X=x,S=1]\\
&=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[(Y(1)-Y(0))C\mid X=x,S=0].
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover,
\[
D(1)-D(0)=C
\qquad P_n^F\text{-almost surely}.
\]
For \(A\in\{D,Y\}\), define the transported contrast using the target covariate density \(f_{\mathrm T}\) by
\[
T_A=\int \Delta_A(x)f_{\mathrm T}(x)\,dx.
\]
The transported first stage equals the target complier share, and the transported outcome contrast equals the target complier-weighted outcome effect:
\[
T_D=\mu=P_n^F(C=1\mid S=0),
\qquad
T_Y=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[(Y(1)-Y(0))C\mid S=0].
\]
The target complier average treatment effect \(\theta\) satisfies
\[
\theta
=\frac{\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[(Y(1)-Y(0))C\mid S=0]}
       {P_n^F(C=1\mid S=0)}
=\frac{T_Y}{T_D}
\in\Theta,
\]
where \(\Theta\) is the effect domain specified by the model.

b5d54ac719c900bc060311afc2942dc62f990359.title: Observable marked density reduction
b5d54ac719c900bc060311afc2942dc62f990359.body:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) and let \(P\) be a transport law. Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Lower density envelope.)} \(0<c_f<1\).
\item \textbf{(Upper density envelope.)} \(1<C_f\).
\item \textbf{(Hölder radius.)} \(1<L\).
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\in\mathcal M_n\) for these constants, as specified in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\end{itemize}
Let \(F\), the seven-coordinate marked density vector, be as in \cref{obj:def:marked-density-vector}, with coordinates indexed by \(0,\ldots,6\). Write \(P_{\mathrm T}\) for the target covariate law and \(P_{\mathrm S}\) for the observed source-record law, whose record consists of covariate \(X\), encouragement \(Z\), receipt \(D\), and outcome \(Y\).

For every measurable \(B\subseteq[0,1]\) and every \(i\in\{0,\ldots,6\}\),
\[
\int_B F_i(x)\,dx
=
\begin{cases}
P_{\mathrm T}(B), & i=0,\\
\displaystyle\int_{\{X\in B\}}(1-Z)\,dP_{\mathrm S}, & i=1,\\
\displaystyle\int_{\{X\in B\}}Z\,dP_{\mathrm S}, & i=2,\\
\displaystyle\int_{\{X\in B\}}(1-Z)Y\,dP_{\mathrm S}, & i=3,\\
\displaystyle\int_{\{X\in B\}}ZY\,dP_{\mathrm S}, & i=4,\\
\displaystyle\int_{\{X\in B\}}(1-Z)D\,dP_{\mathrm S}, & i=5,\\
\displaystyle\int_{\{X\in B\}}ZD\,dP_{\mathrm S}, & i=6.
\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, the source arm densities \(q_0\) and \(q_1\) satisfy
\[
q_0(x)=F_1(x)\ge \frac{c_f}{4},
\qquad
q_1(x)=F_2(x)\ge \frac{c_f}{4},
\qquad x\in[0,1].
\]
For each \(A\in\{Y,D\}\), the transported contrast \(T_A\) and the integrand \(\Phi_A\) of \cref{obj:def:smooth-functional} satisfy
\[
T_A=\int_0^1\Phi_A(F(x))\,dx.
\]

For every \(A\in\{Y,D\}\) and every \(v\in\mathbb R^7\) in the deterministic clipping rectangle
\[
c_f\le v_0\le C_f,\qquad
\frac{c_f}{4}\le v_1,v_2\le\frac{3C_f}{4},\qquad
0\le v_i\le\frac{3C_f}{4}\quad(i=3,\ldots,6),
\]
every order \(k\in\{0,\ldots,4\}\) and every choice of coordinate indices \(i_1,\ldots,i_k\in\{0,\ldots,6\}\) obey
\[
\left|
\frac{\partial^k\Phi_A}{\partial v_{i_1}\cdots\partial v_{i_k}}(v)
\right|
\le
48(1+C_f)^2\left(\frac{4}{c_f}\right)^5.
\]
At order zero, the expression on the left is \(\lvert\Phi_A(v)\rvert\).

b75131819c06c8bf4ae544951aa69375f32ce460.title: Legal mixture and effect separation
b75131819c06c8bf4ae544951aa69375f32ce460.body:
Fix the prescribed noncoverage probability \(\alpha\), density envelopes \(c_f,C_f\), and Hölder radius \(L\), satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Noncoverage.)} \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Lower envelope.)} \(0<c_f<1\).
\item \textbf{(Upper envelope.)} \(1<C_f\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(1<L\).
\end{itemize}
There exists an amplitude \(c_{\star}\in(0,1)\), chosen uniformly in the sample size and strength floor, with the following properties. For every integer \(n\ge n_0=256\) and every \(0<a\le1/4\), set
\[
K_{\mathrm L}=\lceil n^{4/3}\rceil,
\qquad
\bar a=\max\{a,n^{-1/3}\},
\qquad
h_n=c_{\star}K_{\mathrm L}^{-1/8}.
\]
The amplitude satisfies the construction's admissibility conditions
\[
c_{\star}>0,
\qquad
h_n\le\frac{3}{16},
\qquad
h_n^2\le\bar a\left(\frac14-h_n^2\right).
\]

For every \(\tau\in[-1,1]\) and every cellwise sign vector
\(\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}}\), the constructed component
\(Q_{\lambda,\tau}\) belongs to the strength slice
\(\mathcal M_n(a)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:strength-slice}\).
For each \(s\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(x\in[0,1]\), its pointwise conditional-mass averages satisfy
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_{\lambda,\tau}}[C\mid X=x,S=s]=\bar a,
\qquad
\mathbb E_{Q_{\lambda,\tau}}
 [(Y(1)-Y(0))C\mid X=x,S=s]
 =
 -\frac{u_{\lambda}(x)v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)}
 {1/4-u_{\lambda}(x)^2},
\]
where \(C=\mathbf 1\{D(1)>D(0)\}\), \(u_{\lambda}\) is the construction's tiled covariate perturbation, and \(v_{\lambda,\tau}=\tau u_{\lambda}\). These pointwise averages also define versions of the corresponding conditional means under \(Q_{\lambda,\tau}\). Its transported first stage \(\mu\) and target complier effect \(\theta\) satisfy
\[
\mu(Q_{\lambda,\tau})=\bar a,
\qquad
\theta(Q_{\lambda,\tau})=-\frac{\tau J_n}{\bar a},
\]
where the common separation functional \(J_n\) is characterized by
\[
J_n=-\bar a\,\theta(Q_{\lambda,1}).
\]

The unperturbed center \(P_{\star}\) belongs to
\(\mathcal M_n(a)\), and
\[
\mu(P_{\star})=\bar a,
\qquad
\theta(P_{\star})=0,
\qquad
2^{3/4}c_{\star}^2n^{-1/3}
\le J_n\le4c_{\star}^2n^{-1/3}.
\]
For the uniform sign mixture and the center's equal-size observed product experiment,
\[
M_{\tau}
=
2^{-K_{\mathrm L}}
\sum_{\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}}}
\left(Q_{\lambda,\tau,\mathrm S}^{\otimes n}
\otimes Q_{\lambda,\tau,\mathrm T}^{\otimes n}\right),
\qquad
P_{\star}^{(n,n)}
=
P_{\star,\mathrm S}^{\otimes n}
\otimes P_{\star,\mathrm T}^{\otimes n},
\]
the subscripts \(\mathrm S,\mathrm T\) denote the observed source-record and target-covariate laws. Uniformly over \(\tau\in[-1,1]\),
\[
1+\chi^2(M_{\tau},P_{\star}^{(n,n)})
\le
\exp\{C_{\mathrm{mix}}c_{\star}^4\},
\qquad
C_{\mathrm{mix}}=\frac{19321}{1800},
\qquad
\operatorname{TV}(M_{\tau},P_{\star}^{(n,n)})
\le\frac{1-\alpha}{2}.
\]
Moreover, \(M_{\tau}\ll P_{\star}^{(n,n)}\), and its likelihood ratio minus one is square-integrable under \(P_{\star}^{(n,n)}\).

b2405a96ddf9beca64c1f0d000bbc9180be5fb8b.title: Honest upper length envelope
b2405a96ddf9beca64c1f0d000bbc9180be5fb8b.body:
Fix the noncoverage probability \(\alpha\), the density envelopes \(c_f,C_f\), and the Hölder radius \(L\), satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Noncoverage.)} \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Lower density envelope.)} \(0<c_f<1\).
\item \textbf{(Upper density envelope.)} \(1<C_f\).
\item \textbf{(Hölder radius.)} \(1<L\).
\end{itemize}
The score interval \(I_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:score-interval}\) belongs to the class \(\mathfrak H_n\) of honest intervals in \(\cref{obj:def:honest-intervals}\) for every positive integer \(n\).

Set the sample-size threshold to
\[
n_0=256.
\]
Write \(\mu(P)\) for the transported first stage, namely the target-averaged source receipt contrast:
\[
\mu(P)=T_D(P).
\]
There exists a finite constant \(C_0=C_0(\alpha,c_f,C_f,L)>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge n_0\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M_n\), the model class of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\),
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\lambda_{\Theta}(I_n)\right]
\le C_0\min\left\{1,\frac{n^{-1/3}}{\mu(P)}\right\},
\]
where \(\lambda_{\Theta}\) denotes Lebesgue length restricted to the effect domain \(\Theta\), and the expectation is under the joint law of the source and target samples, each of size \(n\).

With the same constant \(C_0\), for every integer \(n\ge n_0\) and every real \(a\) satisfying \(0<a\le 1/4\), the minimax expected-length frontier \(L_n(a)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:length-frontier}\) satisfies
\[
L_n(a)\le C_0\min\left\{1,\frac{n^{-1/3}}{a}\right\}.
\]

c8ab15e2f1480d3fb95f315efc47eb6fd81bacf7.title: Sharp length frontier with elbow
c8ab15e2f1480d3fb95f315efc47eb6fd81bacf7.body:
Fix real constants \(\alpha,c_f,C_f,L\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Noncoverage probability.)} \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Lower density envelope.)} \(0<c_f<1\).
\item \textbf{(Upper density envelope.)} \(1<C_f\).
\item \textbf{(Hölder radius.)} \(1<L\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(I_n\) be the score interval of \cref{obj:def:score-interval}, and let \(L_n(a)\) be the minimax expected restricted length defined in \cref{obj:def:length-frontier}. Set
\[
n_0=256.
\]
There exist finite constants \(0<c_0<C_0\), depending only on \((\alpha,c_f,C_f,L)\), such that \(I_n\in\mathfrak H_n\), the class of honest intervals in \cref{obj:def:honest-intervals}, for every integer \(n>0\), and, for every integer \(n\ge n_0\) and every real \(a\) with \(0<a\le 1/4\),
\[
c_0\min\{1,n^{-1/3}/a\}
\le L_n(a)
\le C_0\min\{1,n^{-1/3}/a\}.
\]
Moreover, for every integer \(n\ge n_0\) and every law \(P\in\mathcal M_n\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, writing
\[
\mu(P)=T_D(P)
\]
for the transported first stage, the same interval sequence satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\lambda_{\Theta}(I_n)\right]
\le C_0\min\{1,n^{-1/3}/\mu(P)\},
\]
where \(\lambda_{\Theta}\) denotes Lebesgue length restricted to the effect domain \(\Theta\).

27fc0e0aa9b10d0e67aa03cac7daa952d6abf740.title: Honest length lower bound
27fc0e0aa9b10d0e67aa03cac7daa952d6abf740.body:
Fix constants satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Coverage.)} The noncoverage probability satisfies \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Density envelopes.)} The lower and upper density envelopes satisfy \(0<c_f<1<C_f\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness.)} The common Hölder radius satisfies \(L>1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathcal M_n\) be the model class in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and let \(\mathcal M_n(a)\) be its strength slice in \(\cref{obj:def:strength-slice}\). Write \(\theta(P)\) for the target-population average treatment effect among compliers under \(P\), and let the effect domain and sample-size threshold be
\[
\Theta=[-1,1],
\qquad n_0=256.
\]
There exists a constant \(c_0=c_0(\alpha,c_f,C_f,L)>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge n_0\) and every \(0<a\le 1/4\), the following holds. Every measurable confidence-set procedure \(C_n\), based on \(n\) source records and \(n\) target covariate records, with \(C_n(\omega)\subseteq\Theta\) for every sample realization \(\omega\), and satisfying
\[
P\bigl(\theta(P)\in C_n\bigr)\ge 1-\alpha
\qquad\text{for every }P\in\mathcal M_n,
\]
obeys
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_n(a)}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\lambda_{\Theta}(C_n)\right]
\ge c_0\min\left\{1,\frac{n^{-1/3}}{a}\right\},
\qquad
\lambda_{\Theta}(C_n)
=\operatorname{Leb}(C_n\cap\Theta).
\]
Here probabilities and expectations are taken under the observed two-sample law. Moreover, the minimax expected-length frontier \(L_n(a)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:length-frontier}\) satisfies
\[
L_n(a)\ge c_0\min\left\{1,\frac{n^{-1/3}}{a}\right\}.
\]

345f5941ac1c08e1ae475b3e681c56ad91b35cd3.title: Target density Hölder regularity
345f5941ac1c08e1ae475b3e681c56ad91b35cd3.body:
The target covariate density \(f_{\mathrm T}\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^\beta([0,1],L)\), with Hölder exponent \(\beta\) and common radius \(L\); explicitly,
\[
\lVert f_{\mathrm T}\rVert_\infty\le L,
\qquad
[f_{\mathrm T}]_\beta\le L.
\]

0e91db51b48929285777435db09360911c3c5b01.title: Source encouragement propensity overlap
0e91db51b48929285777435db09360911c3c5b01.body:
The source encouragement propensity \(e\) satisfies
\[
\frac14\le e(x)\le\frac34
\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
\]

a53b4996acc513359475be2275ce0863a3007890.title: Encouragement propensity Hölder regularity
a53b4996acc513359475be2275ce0863a3007890.body:
The source encouragement propensity \(e\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^\beta([0,1],L)\), with Hölder exponent \(\beta\) and common radius \(L\); explicitly,
\[
\lVert e\rVert_\infty\le L,
\qquad
[e]_\beta\le L.
\]

741fd4e8c2ae6f1364002d2a92436e9ce233dae9.title: Source arm mean regularity
741fd4e8c2ae6f1364002d2a92436e9ce233dae9.body:
For every response \(A\in\{Y,D\}\) and encouragement arm \(z\in\{0,1\}\), the source conditional arm mean \(m_{Az}\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^\beta([0,1],L)\), with Hölder exponent \(\beta\) and common radius \(L\); explicitly, each such arm mean satisfies
\[
\lVert m_{Az}\rVert_\infty\le L,
\qquad
[m_{Az}]_\beta\le L.
\]

08018be73506f1fa5125dc65592ffb3adf050b14.title: Source treatment receipt consistency
08018be73506f1fa5125dc65592ffb3adf050b14.body:
In the source population, observed receipt equals potential receipt under the realized encouragement:
\[
D=D(Z)\qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]

437046a8de7a2dc41990a8b68b9d2b2b706e9ff7.title: Source observed outcome consistency
437046a8de7a2dc41990a8b68b9d2b2b706e9ff7.body:
In the source population, the observed outcome equals the potential outcome under the realized receipt:
\[
Y=Y(D)\qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]

ce3e3fe11154e0c1fd231ad8d74b1606ca7f5337.title: Independent source sampling
ce3e3fe11154e0c1fd231ad8d74b1606ca7f5337.body:
The observed source records \(\mathcal S_n\) are independent and identically distributed with common law \(P_{\mathrm S}\), the law of one observed source record:
\[
\mathcal S_n\sim P_{\mathrm S}^{\otimes n}.
\]

1cf1355ccf5ac9fe52ec8996f416c77d11be51af.title: Independent target sampling
1cf1355ccf5ac9fe52ec8996f416c77d11be51af.body:
The observed target covariate records \(\mathcal T_n\) are independent and identically distributed with common law \(P_{\mathrm T}\), the law of one observed target covariate:
\[
\mathcal T_n\sim P_{\mathrm T}^{\otimes n}.
\]

be99d20126c259cd35f3a1254800eed2e063a848.title: Source–target sample independence
be99d20126c259cd35f3a1254800eed2e063a848.body:
The observed source records \(\mathcal S_n\) and observed target covariate records \(\mathcal T_n\) are independent:
\[
\mathcal S_n\perp\!\!\!\perp\mathcal T_n.
\]

9bac06cbe8216dd063b0e0051b47f26152a33d9e.title: Source density bounds
9bac06cbe8216dd063b0e0051b47f26152a33d9e.body:
The source covariate density \(f_{\mathrm S}\) satisfies the bounds given by \(c_f\), the fixed lower density envelope, and \(C_f\), the fixed upper density envelope, at every point of \(\mathcal X\), the covariate domain:
\[
c_f\le f_{\mathrm S}(x)\le C_f
\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
\]

1b76bf849ea2afdd16640c7c863462ef1f5fe584.title: Target density bounds
1b76bf849ea2afdd16640c7c863462ef1f5fe584.body:
The target covariate density \(f_{\mathrm T}\) satisfies the bounds given by \(c_f\), the fixed lower density envelope, and \(C_f\), the fixed upper density envelope, at every point of \(\mathcal X\), the covariate domain:
\[
c_f\le f_{\mathrm T}(x)\le C_f
\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
\]

973c8fd90ce53dbd6414a0ee9712a757c0ac9da0.title: Source density Hölder regularity
973c8fd90ce53dbd6414a0ee9712a757c0ac9da0.body:
The source covariate density \(f_{\mathrm S}\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^{\beta}([0,1],L)\), the class of continuous functions on \([0,1]\) whose supremum norm and \(\beta\)-Hölder seminorm are bounded by \(L\), where \(\beta\) is the common Hölder exponent and \(L\) is the common Hölder radius:
\[
f_{\mathrm S}\in\mathcal H^{\beta}([0,1],L).
\]
In particular, the two bounds are
\[
\lVert f_{\mathrm S}\rVert_{\infty}\le L,
\qquad
[f_{\mathrm S}]_{\beta}\le L,
\]
where \([f_{\mathrm S}]_{\beta}\) denotes the \(\beta\)-Hölder seminorm of the source density.

c4da0b7725051a39e8d81e7ca467eb3412b8988b.title: Conditional instrument randomization
c4da0b7725051a39e8d81e7ca467eb3412b8988b.body:
Let \(D(z)\) denote potential receipt under encouragement \(z\), and let \(Y(d)\) denote the potential outcome under receipt \(d\). Encouragement \(Z\) is conditionally independent of these potential variables given covariates \(X\) and source membership \(S=1\):
\[
Z\perp\!\!\!\perp (D(0),D(1),Y(0),Y(1))\mid X,S=1.
\]

9968aa5c79aeb19d7cf05f5939b820fbad290e85.title: Exclusion through treatment receipt
9968aa5c79aeb19d7cf05f5939b820fbad290e85.body: For each \(z\in\{0,1\}\), the source potential outcome generated by setting encouragement to \(z\) equals \(Y(D(z))\) almost surely under \(P_n^F\), the primitive full-data law at sample-size index \(n\). Here \(D(z)\) is potential receipt under encouragement \(z\), and \(Y(d)\) is the potential outcome under receipt \(d\).

6b633a0e38b352207bee8312eb5d0fa0058e6e08.title: Monotonicity of treatment receipt
6b633a0e38b352207bee8312eb5d0fa0058e6e08.body:
The potential receipts \(D(1)\) and \(D(0)\), under unit and zero encouragement respectively, satisfy
\[
D(1)\ge D(0)
\]
almost surely under \(P_n^F\), the primitive full-data law at sample-size index \(n\).

82bb38c811ea0f21dc430ef64449bf51ad350aa0.title: Transport of complier outcomes
82bb38c811ea0f21dc430ef64449bf51ad350aa0.body:
Let \(C\) be the indicator of the complier principal stratum, let \(Y(d)\) be the potential outcome under receipt \(d\), and let \(P_n^F\) be the primitive full-data law at sample-size index \(n\). For \(P_{\mathrm T}\)-almost every covariate value \(x\), where \(P_{\mathrm T}\) is the law of one observed target covariate,
\[
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[(Y(1)-Y(0))C\mid X=x,S=0]
=
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[(Y(1)-Y(0))C\mid X=x,S=1],
\]
where \(S=0\) denotes target membership and \(S=1\) denotes source membership.

20a3d96b85fd092f70082f1f1c61f3bdbfb9a20b.title: Transport of complier shares
20a3d96b85fd092f70082f1f1c61f3bdbfb9a20b.body:
Let \(C\) be the indicator of the complier principal stratum, and let \(P_n^F\) be the primitive full-data law at sample-size index \(n\). For \(P_{\mathrm T}\)-almost every covariate value \(x\), where \(P_{\mathrm T}\) is the law of one observed target covariate,
\[
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[C\mid X=x,S=0]
=
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[C\mid X=x,S=1],
\]
where \(S=0\) denotes target membership and \(S=1\) denotes source membership.

24f1fac837bd34f66c0f3e80173b46b6a5c2f98c.title: Positive transported first stage
24f1fac837bd34f66c0f3e80173b46b6a5c2f98c.body:
The transported compliance share and first stage, \(\mu\), satisfies
\[
\mu>0.
\]

6e187916baa07985e5ee8cd1972842e2c1d86882.title: Marked-density vector \(F\)
6e187916baa07985e5ee8cd1972842e2c1d86882.body:
The marked-density vector for the model in \cref{obj:def:model-class} is
\[
F(x)=\bigl(f_{\mathrm T}(x),q_0(x),q_1(x),
r_{Y0}(x),r_{Y1}(x),r_{D0}(x),r_{D1}(x)\bigr),
\]
where the source arm densities and response-marked arm densities are
\[
q_z(x)=f_{\mathrm S}(x)P_{\mathrm S}(Z=z\mid X=x),
\qquad
r_{Az}(x)=q_z(x)m_{Az}(x),
\qquad A\in\{Y,D\},\quad z\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Here \(m_{Az}(x)\) is the source conditional mean of response \(A\) in encouragement arm \(z\).

962323c50c7d8961b5fa09bdb1cc794ac5bd1b8e.title: Transported contrast functional \(T_A\)
962323c50c7d8961b5fa09bdb1cc794ac5bd1b8e.body:
The target-averaged source contrast for response \(A\in\{Y,D\}\) is
\[
T_A=\int_0^1\Phi_A(F(x))\,dx,
\qquad
\Phi_A(F)=f_{\mathrm T}
\left(\frac{r_{A1}}{q_1}-\frac{r_{A0}}{q_0}\right).
\]

d896a37baabf3435dfae7bc80f15f7fa4a51e4f8.title: Cubic estimator \(\widehat T_A\)
d896a37baabf3435dfae7bc80f15f7fa4a51e4f8.body:
For \(A\in\{Y,D\}\), the inputs are the sample size \(n\), the threshold \(n_0\), the deterministic sample-channel blocks \(\mathcal B_b^G\) of sizes \(m_b\), the dyadic resolution maps \(K_0(n),K_2(n),K_3(n)\), the normalized marked histograms \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}\), the clipped pilot vector \(\widehat F\), the histogram residuals \(R_{i,K}^{(b)}\), the seven-coordinate index set \(\mathcal I\), the coordinate channels \(g(i)\), the observable marks \(W_{i,r}\), and the observed covariates \(X_r^{g(i)}\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item For \(n\ge n_0\), set the resolutions and cell midpoints to
\[
K_0=K_0(n),\qquad K_2=K_2(n),\qquad K_3=K_3(n),
\qquad
x_{\ell,K}=\frac{\ell-\tfrac12}{K},
\quad \ell=1,\ldots,K.
\]
The resolutions satisfy \(K_0\mid K_3\) and \(K_3\mid K_2\).

\item For \(n\ge n_0\), form the observable linear correction
\[
\mathsf L_A=
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
\left\{
\frac{1}{m_1}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_1^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,\partial_i\Phi_A
\bigl(\widehat F(X_r^{g(i)})\bigr)
-
\int_0^1
\partial_i\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\widehat F_i(x)\,dx
\right\}.
\]

\item For \(n\ge n_0\), form the observable quadratic correction
\[
\mathsf Q_A=
\frac{1}{2K_2}
\sum_{i,j\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_2}
\partial_{ij}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_2}))
R_{i,K_2}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_2})
R_{j,K_2}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_2}).
\]

\item For \(n\ge n_0\), form the observable cubic correction
\[
\mathsf C_A=
\frac{1}{6K_3}
\sum_{i,j,k\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_3}
\partial_{ijk}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_3}))
R_{i,K_3}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{j,K_3}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{k,K_3}^{(3)}(x_{\ell,K_3}).
\]
Repeated coordinate indices use distinct evaluation blocks.

\item Output
\[
\widehat T_A=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\int_0^1\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\,dx+
\mathsf L_A+\mathsf Q_A+\mathsf C_A,
& n\ge n_0,\\
0,& n<n_0.
\end{cases}
\]
Every integral is an exact finite sum, with \(K_0\mid K_3\) and \(K_3\mid K_2\). For \(n<n_0\), the score interval takes the finite-size fallback
\[
I_n=\Theta.
\]
\end{enumerate}

0a30e3768cc52e183395f000ebd6eba46190bab2.title: Inverted score interval \(I_n\)
0a30e3768cc52e183395f000ebd6eba46190bab2.body:
The inverted score interval is
\[
I_n=
\begin{cases}
\Theta,& n<n_0,\\
\mathcal A_n,& n\ge n_0\ \text{and}\ \mathcal A_n\ne\varnothing,\\
\{0\},& n\ge n_0\ \text{and}\ \mathcal A_n=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\mathcal A_n\) is the calibrated affine-score acceptance set, \(\Theta\) is the bounded effect domain, and \(n_0\) is the threshold for using the cubic estimator.

2d4b16acd9540ccda1b3919d21dc7de871bf5574.title: Honest interval class \(\mathfrak H_n\)
2d4b16acd9540ccda1b3919d21dc7de871bf5574.body:
The class of uniformly honest connected intervals is
\[
\mathfrak H_n=
\left\{
C_n:
C_n\subseteq\Theta\ \text{is a measurable connected interval},
\quad
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_n}P(\theta\in C_n)\ge 1-\alpha
\right\}.
\]
Here \(\Theta\) is the bounded domain of the target-population complier effect \(\theta\), \(\mathcal M_n\) is the model class, and \(\alpha\) is the prescribed noncoverage probability.

ba952419430adae9ecf10d871d79ce839e0d8939.title: First-stage strength slice \(\mathcal M_n(a)\)
ba952419430adae9ecf10d871d79ce839e0d8939.body:
The first-stage strength slice is
\[
\mathcal M_n(a)=
\left\{P\in\mathcal M_n:a\le\mu(P)\le\frac14\right\},
\qquad n\ge n_0,\quad 0<a\le\frac14.
\]
Here \(\mu(P)\) is the transported compliance share under \(P\), \(\mathcal M_n\) is the model class, and \(n_0\) is the threshold for using the cubic estimator.

066e2e3da63763cdbf4b508e99fe759aaf45a950.title: Model class $\mathcal M_n$
066e2e3da63763cdbf4b508e99fe759aaf45a950.body:
The model class \(\mathcal M_n\) consists of law triples
\[
P=(P_n^F,P_{\mathrm S},P_{\mathrm T}),
\]
where \(P_n^F\) is the primitive full-data law, \(P_{\mathrm S}\) is the law of one observed source record, and \(P_{\mathrm T}\) is the law of one observed target covariate, satisfying all of the following restrictions at sample-size index \(n\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} \cref{obj:ass:source-iid,obj:ass:target-iid,obj:ass:sample-independence}.
\item \textbf{(Covariate densities.)} \cref{obj:ass:source-density-bounds,obj:ass:target-density-bounds,obj:ass:source-density-holder,obj:ass:target-density-holder}.
\item \textbf{(Propensity and arm means.)} \cref{obj:ass:propensity-overlap,obj:ass:propensity-holder,obj:ass:arm-means-holder}.
\item \textbf{(Causal restrictions.)} \cref{obj:ass:receipt-consistency,obj:ass:outcome-consistency,obj:ass:instrument-randomization,obj:ass:exclusion,obj:ass:monotonicity}.
\item \textbf{(Transport and strength.)} \cref{obj:ass:transport-complier-outcome,obj:ass:transport-complier-share,obj:ass:positive-strength}.
\end{itemize}

b721e75677368467530f79e8cdc8b37d14c8084f.title: Fixed-geometry subclass $\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{fix}}(\mathcal G)$
b721e75677368467530f79e8cdc8b37d14c8084f.body:
The fixed-geometry subclass is
\[
\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{fix}}(\mathcal G)
=
\bigl\{P\in\mathcal M_n:(f_{\mathrm S},f_{\mathrm T},e)=\mathcal G\bigr\},
\]
with equality at sample-size index \(n\). Here \(\mathcal G\) is the supplied triple of source covariate density \(f_{\mathrm S}\), target covariate density \(f_{\mathrm T}\), and source encouragement propensity \(e\). Membership in \(\mathcal M_n\) requires all of the following restrictions at that index:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} \cref{obj:ass:source-iid,obj:ass:target-iid,obj:ass:sample-independence}.
\item \textbf{(Covariate densities.)} \cref{obj:ass:source-density-bounds,obj:ass:target-density-bounds,obj:ass:source-density-holder,obj:ass:target-density-holder}.
\item \textbf{(Propensity and arm means.)} \cref{obj:ass:propensity-overlap,obj:ass:propensity-holder,obj:ass:arm-means-holder}.
\item \textbf{(Causal restrictions.)} \cref{obj:ass:receipt-consistency,obj:ass:outcome-consistency,obj:ass:instrument-randomization,obj:ass:exclusion,obj:ass:monotonicity}.
\item \textbf{(Transport and strength.)} \cref{obj:ass:transport-complier-outcome,obj:ass:transport-complier-share,obj:ass:positive-strength}.
\end{itemize}

c7fc8a8374f9d6d62409b69a72ed3ba5246730e1.title: Supplied-geometry score $\widetilde T_A^{\mathcal G}$
c7fc8a8374f9d6d62409b69a72ed3ba5246730e1.body:
For \(A\in\{Y,D\}\) and every positive integer \(n\), the supplied-geometry score is
\[
\widetilde T_A^{\mathcal G}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{f_{\mathrm T}^0(X_i)}{f_{\mathrm S}^0(X_i)}
\left\{
\frac{Z_iA_i}{e^0(X_i)}
-
\frac{(1-Z_i)A_i}{1-e^0(X_i)}
\right\}.
\]
Here \((X_i,Z_i,D_i,Y_i)\) are the observed source records, comprising covariates, encouragement, receipt, and outcome, and the supplied geometry is
\[
\mathcal G=(f_{\mathrm S}^0,f_{\mathrm T}^0,e^0),
\]
where \(f_{\mathrm S}^0\) and \(f_{\mathrm T}^0\) are the supplied source and target covariate densities and \(e^0\) is the supplied source encouragement propensity. The statistic is a function of the observed source sample and \(\mathcal G\) alone.

f3a3610233ef98b3777184d977fee69c9299f086.title: Supplied-geometry interval $I_n^{\mathcal G}$

a83c725a5d86ba82e67d9892d6fafef72127267e.title: Finite-cell subclass $\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{cell}}(\Pi)$
a83c725a5d86ba82e67d9892d6fafef72127267e.body:
The finite-cell subclass \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{cell}}(\Pi)\) consists of the laws \(P\in\mathcal M_n\) whose source covariate density \(f_{\mathrm S}\), target covariate density \(f_{\mathrm T}\), and source encouragement propensity \(e\) are constant on every cell of the fixed finite interval partition \(\Pi\), at sample-size index \(n\). Membership in \(\mathcal M_n\) requires all of the following restrictions at that index:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} \cref{obj:ass:source-iid,obj:ass:target-iid,obj:ass:sample-independence}.
\item \textbf{(Covariate densities.)} \cref{obj:ass:source-density-bounds,obj:ass:target-density-bounds,obj:ass:source-density-holder,obj:ass:target-density-holder}.
\item \textbf{(Propensity and arm means.)} \cref{obj:ass:propensity-overlap,obj:ass:propensity-holder,obj:ass:arm-means-holder}.
\item \textbf{(Causal restrictions.)} \cref{obj:ass:receipt-consistency,obj:ass:outcome-consistency,obj:ass:instrument-randomization,obj:ass:exclusion,obj:ass:monotonicity}.
\item \textbf{(Transport and strength.)} \cref{obj:ass:transport-complier-outcome,obj:ass:transport-complier-share,obj:ass:positive-strength}.
\end{itemize}

83ca3b7b4927da1a8438f461725b42e72bd65deb.title: Continuous-geometry laws $P_{\sigma}^{\dagger}$
83ca3b7b4927da1a8438f461725b42e72bd65deb.body:
For each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), the full-data law \(P_{\sigma}^{\dagger}\) is specified by the following covariate densities, principal-stratum distribution, potential variables, and sampling scheme. Define the perturbation amplitude by
\[
\varepsilon_{\dagger}
=
\frac14\min\{1-c_f,C_f-1,1/4,L-1\},
\]
where \(c_f\) and \(C_f\) are the fixed lower and upper density envelopes and \(L\) is the common Hölder radius. With \(g_{\dagger}\) denoting the covariate perturbation, set
\[
f_{\mathrm S}(x)=1+\sigma\varepsilon_{\dagger}g_{\dagger}(x),
\qquad
f_{\mathrm T}(x)=1-\sigma\varepsilon_{\dagger}g_{\dagger}(x),
\qquad
e(x)=\frac12+\sigma\varepsilon_{\dagger}g_{\dagger}(x).
\]
The law is completed as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Principal strata.)} Conditional on \(X\) in each population, the complier, always-taker, and never-taker probabilities are, respectively,
\[
\frac18,\qquad \frac7{16},\qquad \frac7{16}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Potential variables.)} The potential receipts \(D(0)\) and \(D(1)\) are the receipts corresponding to the assigned principal stratum, and the potential outcomes satisfy
\[
Y(0)=Y(1)=\frac12.
\]
\item \textbf{(Source observations.)} Draw encouragement \(Z\) conditionally independently of the potential variables given \(X\), with propensity \(e(X)\), and observe
\[
D=D(Z),\qquad Y=Y(D).
\]
\item \textbf{(Samples.)} Generate independent source and target samples with covariate densities \(f_{\mathrm S}\) and \(f_{\mathrm T}\), respectively.
\end{itemize}
For the combined full-data representation of these two conditional population laws, the population indicator \(S\) has probabilities
\[
P_{\sigma}^{\dagger}(S=\mathrm{source})
=
P_{\sigma}^{\dagger}(S=\mathrm{target})
=
\frac12.
\]
These probabilities specify the representation convention for \(P_{\sigma}^{\dagger}\); the ambient model class retains its stated assumptions.

2a3bbd9ba301970c2a7cdd48c2dc71a01e6b08bf.title: Minimax length frontier \(L_n(a)\)
2a3bbd9ba301970c2a7cdd48c2dc71a01e6b08bf.body:
The minimax expected-length frontier is
\[
L_n(a)
=
\inf_{C_n\in\mathfrak H_n}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_n(a)}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\lambda_{\Theta}(C_n)\right],
\qquad n\ge n_0,\quad 0<a\le\frac14,
\]
where \(\mathfrak H_n\) is the class of uniformly honest connected intervals, \(\mathcal M_n(a)\) is the model slice with transported first stage between \(a\) and \(1/4\), and \(\lambda_{\Theta}\) denotes Lebesgue length restricted to the effect domain \(\Theta\).

1648b0f752610dca7e3aa136ed0e28010d170665.title: IV mixture \(M_{\tau}\)
1648b0f752610dca7e3aa136ed0e28010d170665.body:
For \(n\ge n_0\), \(0<a\le1/4\), a positive integer \(K_{\mathrm L}\) counting perturbation cells, an amplitude \(c_{\star}\), a sign vector \(\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}}\), and a continuum index \(\tau\in[-1,1]\), construct the mixture as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Set the baseline compliance share and perturbation height to
\[
b=\bar a=\max\{a,n^{-1/3}\},
\qquad
h=h_n=c_{\star}K_{\mathrm L}^{-1/8},
\qquad
v_{\lambda,\tau}=\tau u_{\lambda},
\]
where \(u_{\lambda}\) is the tiled covariate perturbation indexed by the cell signs. Define admissibility by
\[
\operatorname{Adm}_{n,a}(c_{\star})
\Longleftrightarrow
\left(
0<c_{\star}
\ \text{and}\
h\le\frac{3}{16}
\ \text{and}\
h^2\le b\left(\frac14-h^2\right)
\right).
\]
Perform the remaining steps when \(\operatorname{Adm}_{n,a}(c_{\star})\) holds.

\item Define the source and target covariate densities and encouragement probabilities by
\[
f_{\mathrm S}=1,
\qquad
f_{\mathrm T}=1+u_{\lambda},
\qquad
e_1^{(\lambda)}=\frac12+u_{\lambda},
\qquad
e_0^{(\lambda)}=\frac12-u_{\lambda}.
\]
For \(z,d,y\in\{0,1\}\), define the source joint conditional cells by the exact formula
\[
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(Z=z,D=d,Y=y\mid X=x)
=
e_z^{(\lambda)}(x)R_z^{(b)}(d,y)
+\frac{v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)(2y-1)}4,
\]
where \(R_z^{(b)}(d,y)\) is the baseline receipt–outcome cell probability at compliance share \(b\). The cells conditional on encouragement and covariates are
\[
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(D=d,Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x)
=
\frac{
e_z^{(\lambda)}(x)R_z^{(b)}(d,y)
+v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)(2y-1)/4
}{
e_z^{(\lambda)}(x)
}.
\]

\item Let \(C\) denote the complier indicator, and let \(Y(d)\) denote the potential outcome under receipt state \(d\). Define the complier outcome margins by
\[
M_{1y}(x)
=
P(C=1,Y(1)=y\mid X=x)
=
\frac b2
-
\frac{(2y-1)u_{\lambda}(x)v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)}
{2\{1/4-u_{\lambda}(x)^2\}},
\]
\[
M_{0y}(x)
=
P(C=1,Y(0)=y\mid X=x)
=
\frac b2
+
\frac{(2y-1)u_{\lambda}(x)v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)}
{2\{1/4-u_{\lambda}(x)^2\}},
\qquad y\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Assign always-takers and never-takers the conditional masses
\[
P(D(0)=D(1)=1,Y(1)=y\mid X=x)
=
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(D=1,Y=y\mid Z=0,X=x),
\]
\[
P(D(0)=D(1)=0,Y(0)=y\mid X=x)
=
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(D=0,Y=y\mid Z=1,X=x),
\]
where \(D(z)\) denotes potential receipt under encouragement \(z\). For compliers, set
\[
P(Y(d)=y\mid X=x,C=1)
=
\frac{M_{dy}(x)}b,
\qquad d,y\in\{0,1\},
\]
and couple \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently under these binary marginals. Set
\[
Y(0)=0\quad\text{for always-takers},
\qquad
Y(1)=0\quad\text{for never-takers}.
\]

\item Draw encouragement conditionally independently of the potential receipts and outcomes:
\[
Z\ \perp\ (D(0),D(1),Y(0),Y(1))\mid X,
\qquad
P(Z=1\mid X=x)=e_1^{(\lambda)}(x).
\]
Observe
\[
D=D(Z),
\qquad
Y=Y(D).
\]
Use the same conditional primitive full-data law given \(X\) in source and target. Represent the resulting combined law \(Q_{\lambda,\tau}\) using
\[
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(S=\mathrm{source})
=
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(S=\mathrm{target})
=
\frac12.
\]
This source–target allocation is a convention for representing the constructed law. Admissibility restricts the parameters of this construction.

\item Define the center law by
\[
P_{\star}
=
\left.Q_{\lambda,\tau}\right|_{u_{\lambda}=v_{\lambda,\tau}=0},
\]
retaining the baseline compliance share \(b\) and the representation convention
\[
P_{\star}(S=\mathrm{source})
=
P_{\star}(S=\mathrm{target})
=
\frac12.
\]
Its observed product experiment consists of independent source and target samples, each of size \(n\):
\[
P_{\star}^{(n,n)}
=
(P_{\star,\mathrm S})^{\otimes n}
\otimes
(P_{\star,\mathrm T})^{\otimes n},
\]
where \(P_{\star,\mathrm S}\) and \(P_{\star,\mathrm T}\) are its one-record observed source and target laws.

\item Output the uniform sign mixture of the independent source–target product experiments:
\[
M_{\tau}
=
2^{-K_{\mathrm L}}
\sum_{\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}}}
(Q_{\lambda,\tau,\mathrm S})^{\otimes n}
\otimes
(Q_{\lambda,\tau,\mathrm T})^{\otimes n},
\]
where \(Q_{\lambda,\tau,\mathrm S}\) and \(Q_{\lambda,\tau,\mathrm T}\) are the one-record observed source and target laws induced by \(Q_{\lambda,\tau}\).
\end{enumerate}

1a21ec63b34e2b3141348fe23946aa556c5fb8d6.title: Unequal-sample frontier \(R_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}(a)\)
1a21ec63b34e2b3141348fe23946aa556c5fb8d6.body:
The unequal-sample minimax expected-length frontier is
\[
R_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}(a)
=
\inf_{C_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}\in
\mathfrak H^{\mathrm u}_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm u}_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}(a)}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\lambda_{\Theta}\!\left(C_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}\right)
\right],
\qquad
0<a\le\frac14,
\]
for positive integers \(N_{\mathrm S}\) and \(N_{\mathrm T}\), where \(\lambda_{\Theta}\) denotes Lebesgue length restricted to the effect domain \(\Theta\).

Here \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm u}_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}\) is the class of full-data and one-record observed-law triples satisfying every law-level density, smoothness, overlap, causal, transport, and positive-strength condition of the equal-sample model class \(\mathcal M_n\), observed under
\[
P_{\mathrm S}^{\otimes N_{\mathrm S}}
\otimes
P_{\mathrm T}^{\otimes N_{\mathrm T}},
\]
where \(P_{\mathrm S}\) is the law of one observed source record and \(P_{\mathrm T}\) is the law of one observed target covariate. The independent source and target samples contain \(N_{\mathrm S}\) records \((X,Z,D,Y)\) and \(N_{\mathrm T}\) records \(X\), respectively. With \(\mu(P)\) denoting the transported first stage, the strength slice is
\[
\mathcal M^{\mathrm u}_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}(a)
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm u}_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}:
a\le\mu(P)\le\frac14
\right\}.
\]

Let \(C_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}\) range over measurable connected random intervals contained in \(\Theta\) and based on this product experiment. With \(\theta(P)\) denoting the target-population average treatment effect among compliers and \(\alpha\) the prescribed noncoverage probability, define
\[
\mathfrak H^{\mathrm u}_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}
=
\left\{
C_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}:
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm u}_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}}
P\!\left(
\theta(P)\in C_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}
\right)
\ge1-\alpha
\right\}.
\]

60c0df93db10a9636977a840eaa7191ae915c654.title: Unequal-sample length phases
60c0df93db10a9636977a840eaa7191ae915c654.body: What is the exact piecewise order of \(R_{N_{\mathrm S},N_{\mathrm T}}(a)\), the unequal-sample minimax expected-length frontier, when the source sample size \(N_{\mathrm S}\) and target sample size \(N_{\mathrm T}\) diverge at unrelated rates? Can a single finite-sample honest interval attain this order in every phase, together with a matching legal instrumental-variable lower family satisfying the no-defiers restriction?

ce5b253e06a4d891b8d5f5d7470f1f12c8456330.title: Expected random-set length
ce5b253e06a4d891b8d5f5d7470f1f12c8456330.body:
Let \(C_n\subseteq\Theta\) be a measurable random set under \(P\), where \(\Theta\) is the effect domain and \(\lambda_{\Theta}\) denotes Lebesgue length restricted to that domain. Then
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\lambda_{\Theta}(C_n)\right]
=
\int_{\Theta}P(t\in C_n)\,dt.
\]

67ed4fda3ac16442e24684d8e00c6d49dcddf6ba.title: The scalar covariate space
67ed4fda3ac16442e24684d8e00c6d49dcddf6ba.body:
The covariate space is
\[
\mathcal X := [0,1] \subset \mathbb R.
\]

ad9fc54154f52fd4e5f0f0560544f46520d92a75.title: Deterministic sample block
ad9fc54154f52fd4e5f0f0560544f46520d92a75.body:
The deterministic block \(\mathcal B_b^G\) in sample channel \(G\), for sample size \(n\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\) and block index \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), is
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
i\in\mathbb Z:
0\le i<n,\quad
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le i<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\}.
\]

cf787ec19b197ede1364a5d032eb419f016de745.title: Exact block size
cf787ec19b197ede1364a5d032eb419f016de745.body:
The block size \(m_b\), for a nonnegative integer \(n\) and an index \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), is defined by
\[
m_b := \max\left\{
\left\lfloor \frac{(b+1)n}{4} \right\rfloor
-
\left\lfloor \frac{bn}{4} \right\rfloor,
0
\right\}.
\]

cc65ebaa1a9ee17c4052306c34f0a13353b8f5ce.title: Dyadic pilot resolution rule
cc65ebaa1a9ee17c4052306c34f0a13353b8f5ce.body:
The pilot resolution \(K_0(n)\), for sample size \(n\in\mathbb N\), is defined by
\[
K_0(n)=
\begin{cases}
1, & n<n_0,\\[2pt]
2^{\left\lfloor \frac45\,\frac{\log m_0}{\log 2}\right\rfloor},
& n\ge n_0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(n_0\) is the threshold for using the cubic estimator and \(m_0\) is the size of block \(0\) at sample size \(n\).

d9727be418d54105193d3736d7fdf287f7932cde.title: Quadratic correction resolution
d9727be418d54105193d3736d7fdf287f7932cde.body:
The quadratic resolution \(K_2(n)\), for \(n\in\mathbb N\), is defined by
\[
K_2(n)=
\begin{cases}
1, & n<n_0,\\[2pt]
2^{\left\lfloor \frac{4}{3}\,\frac{\log m_0}{\log 2}\right\rfloor},
& n\ge n_0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(n_0\) is the threshold and \(m_0\) is the size of block \(0\) at sample size \(n\). The floor is taken in the nonnegative integers, with value \(0\) when its argument is negative.

042c0f22bf2c785478915f7e86232f33e6906213.title: Cubic correction resolution
042c0f22bf2c785478915f7e86232f33e6906213.body:
The cubic resolution \(K_3(n)\), for \(n\in\mathbb N\), is defined by
\[
K_3(n)=
\begin{cases}
1, & n<n_0,\\[2pt]
2^{\left\lfloor \dfrac{\log m_0}{\log 2}\right\rfloor}, & n\ge n_0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(n_0\) is the threshold for using the cubic estimator and \(m_0\) is the size of block \(0\) at sample size \(n\). The floor is taken in the nonnegative integers, with value \(0\) when its argument is negative; the logarithm at \(0\) is assigned value \(0\).

39e26e4ca4414e988c95c3cbca6822812d36d76a.title: Blockwise marked histograms
39e26e4ca4414e988c95c3cbca6822812d36d76a.body:
The marked histogram \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}\), for two samples \(\mathcal S_n\) and \(\mathcal T_n\) of \(n\) source records and \(n\) target covariates, coordinate \(i\in\{0,\ldots,6\}\), resolution \(K\in\{0,1,\ldots\}\), block \(b\in\{0,\ldots,3\}\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\), is
\[
H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)=
\begin{cases}
0, & n<256,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{K}{m_b}
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K-1}
\mathbf 1\{x\in\text{cell }\ell\}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in\text{cell }\ell\},
& n\ge256.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(K\ge1\), cell \(\ell\), with \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), is
\[
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K,(\ell+1)/K), & \ell<K-1,\\
[\ell/K,1], & \ell=K-1.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(K=0\), the sum over cells is empty and equals zero. For either sample channel \(G\), the deterministic block and its size are
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le r<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\},
\qquad
m_b=
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
-
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
The sample channel \(g(i)\) is the target channel for \(i=0\) and the source channel for \(i=1,\ldots,6\); \(X_r^{g(i)}\) is the corresponding observed covariate.

The observable mark \(W_{0,r}\) is \(1\). For source record \(r\), \(W_{1,r}\) and \(W_{2,r}\) are the indicators of zero and unit encouragement, respectively. The marks \(W_{3,r}\) and \(W_{4,r}\) multiply these respective encouragement indicators by the observed outcome clipped to \([0,1]\), whose value is \(\max\{0,\min\{1,\text{observed outcome of record }r\}\}\). The marks \(W_{5,r}\) and \(W_{6,r}\) multiply the respective zero- and unit-encouragement indicators by the indicator of treatment receipt.

236514cc0d406da81f87fc59c66ef9ca854a6337.title: Clipped marked-density pilot
236514cc0d406da81f87fc59c66ef9ca854a6337.body:
The pilot vector \(\widehat F(x)\), for real envelope parameters \(c_f,C_f\), a sample-size index \(n\in\mathbb N\), two samples \((\mathcal S_n,\mathcal T_n)\) of size \(n\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\), is defined as follows. For \(n<256\),
\[
\widehat F(x)=\left(1,\frac12,\frac12,0,0,0,0\right).
\]
For \(n\ge256\), use the dyadic pilot resolution \(K_0(n)\) with exponent \(4/5\). For each coordinate \(i\in\{0,\ldots,6\}\), form the marked histogram on block \(0\),
\[
H_{i,K_0(n)}^{(0)}(x)
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K_0(n)-1}
\mathbf 1\{x\in\text{cell }\ell\}
\frac{K_0(n)}{m_0}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_0^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in\text{cell }\ell\},
\]
where the cells are those of the resolution-\(K_0(n)\) partition, \(g(i)\) selects the coordinate's sample channel, \(W_{i,r}\) is its observable mark, and \(m_0\) is the size of block \(0\). Define \(\widehat F_i(x)\) by clipping this histogram value with lower and upper cutoffs
\[
\begin{cases}
c_f,\ C_f, & i=0,\\
c_f/4,\ 3C_f/4, & i\in\{1,2\},\\
0,\ 3C_f/4, & i\in\{3,4,5,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]

4569a18a75fd6aa18a84e9b52b9e82d097a64ee9.title: Marked histogram residual
4569a18a75fd6aa18a84e9b52b9e82d097a64ee9.body:
The residual \(R_{i,K}^{(b)}\) is the block-specific marked histogram minus the corresponding coordinate of the clipped pilot:
\[
R_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)
=
H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)-\widehat F_i(x).
\]
Here \(n\) and \(K\) are arbitrary nonnegative integers, the data consist of \(n\) source records and \(n\) target covariates, \(i\) indexes the seven coordinates, \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), \(x\in\mathbb R\), and \(c_f,C_f\in\mathbb R\) are the supplied pilot-clipping parameters. For \(n<n_0\), the marked histogram is zero and
\[
\widehat F(x)=(1,1/2,1/2,0,0,0,0).
\]
For \(n\ge n_0\), \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)\) is the sum over resolution-\(K\) cells containing \(x\) of \(K/m_b\) times the sum of marks \(W_{i,r}\) for records \(r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}\) whose covariates lie in that same cell. The pilot coordinate \(\widehat F_i(x)\) is obtained by applying the coordinate-specific clipping rule with parameters \(c_f,C_f\) to \(H_{i,K_0(n)}^{(0)}(x)\).

412960820652f33a0a5ad3cae82032609191d1d9.title: Calibrated score acceptance set
412960820652f33a0a5ad3cae82032609191d1d9.body:
The calibrated affine-score acceptance set \(\mathcal A_n\) is defined, for real inputs \(\alpha,c_f,C_f,L\), a sample size \(n\in\mathbb N\), and a pair of source and target samples each containing \(n\) records, by
\[
\mathcal A_n
=
\left\{
\theta\in[-1,1]:
\left|\widehat T_Y-\theta\widehat T_D\right|
\le
2\sqrt{\frac{2C_{\mathrm{mse}}}{\alpha}}\,
n^{-1/3}
\right\}.
\]
Here \(\widehat T_Y\) and \(\widehat T_D\) are the cubic estimators computed from the supplied samples with inputs \(c_f,C_f\), and \(C_{\mathrm{mse}}\) is the mean-square envelope evaluated at \(c_f,C_f,L\). Each cubic estimator equals zero when \(n<n_0\), the estimator threshold, and otherwise equals its pilot integral plus its linear, quadratic, and cubic corrections. The square root and negative power use their total real-valued conventions, including at zero.

fa1afecfcefc03c021a4e479ea49e8c048522c4d.title: Known geometry calibration radius

d129a8bd87dc9205f36e930e417b8152ed173288.title: Coupled tiled perturbation
d129a8bd87dc9205f36e930e417b8152ed173288.body:
The coupled perturbation \(u_{\lambda}(x)\), with parameters \(c_{\star},\tau\in\mathbb R\), \(n\in\mathbb N\), cellwise signs \(\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}}\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\), is defined by
\[
u_{\lambda}(x)
=
\tau\sum_{\ell=0}^{K_{\mathrm L}-1}
\begin{cases}
h_n\lambda_\ell\,
\operatorname{bump}(K_{\mathrm L}x-\ell),
& x\in\operatorname{cell}(K_{\mathrm L},\ell),\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
K_{\mathrm L}=\left\lceil n^{4/3}\right\rceil,
\qquad
h_n=c_{\star}K_{\mathrm L}^{-1/8}.
\]
Here the cell and bump functions are those supplied for the tiled perturbation, and \(\lambda_\ell\) is the sign value of the supplied Boolean entry for cell \(\ell\).

44b15fe88f821d4d2af5a2830649914cf469b343.title: Centered covariate witness direction
44b15fe88f821d4d2af5a2830649914cf469b343.body:
The witness direction \(g_{\dagger}\) is defined, for every \(x\in\mathbb R\), by
\[
g_{\dagger}(x)
=
\left|x-\frac12\right|^{1/8}
-
\int_0^1 \left|u-\frac12\right|^{1/8}\,du.
\]

ecb1830147802ea6efbf9a0761d7775c20727a03.title: Source density Hölder regularity
ecb1830147802ea6efbf9a0761d7775c20727a03.body:
The source covariate density \(f_{\mathrm S}\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^{\beta}([0,1],L)\), the class of continuous functions on \([0,1]\) with supremum norm and \(\beta\)-Hölder seminorm bounded separately by \(L\), where \(\beta\) is the common Hölder exponent and \(L\) is the common Hölder radius:
\[
\beta=\frac18,\qquad L>1,\qquad
f_{\mathrm S}\in\mathcal H^{\beta}([0,1],L).
\]
Thus the bounds are
\[
\lVert f_{\mathrm S}\rVert_{\infty}\le L,
\qquad
[f_{\mathrm S}]_{\beta}\le L,
\]
where \([f_{\mathrm S}]_{\beta}\) denotes the \(\beta\)-Hölder seminorm of the source density.

2e6ccd2aea3b584d32e62ca49d1fa0161a96d28f.title: Target covariate density bounds
2e6ccd2aea3b584d32e62ca49d1fa0161a96d28f.body:
The target covariate law \(P_{\mathrm T}\), with target density \(f_{\mathrm T}\), satisfies the following conditions on \(\mathcal X=[0,1]\), the covariate domain, with real constants \(c_f\) and \(C_f\), the lower and upper density envelopes:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Density identity.)} For every Borel set \(B\subseteq\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{\mathrm T}(B)=\int_{B\cap\mathcal X}\max\{f_{\mathrm T}(x),0\}\,dx.
\]
\item \textbf{(Density envelope.)} For every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
c_f\le f_{\mathrm T}(x)\le C_f.
\]
\item \textbf{(Positive lower envelope.)}
\[
0<c_f.
\]
\end{itemize}

1308fc8aab32c6d5be21088b0ff2ccf01c70a66a.title: Source density and support bounds
1308fc8aab32c6d5be21088b0ff2ccf01c70a66a.body:
The source covariate density \(f_{\mathrm S}\), with \(c_f\) and \(C_f\) the fixed lower and upper density envelopes, satisfies the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Envelope constants.)} \(0<c_f<1<C_f\).
\item \textbf{(Full-data law and support.)} \(P_n^F\), the full-data law, is a probability law. Under this law, the covariate \(X\) and both potential outcomes \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) belong to \([0,1]\) almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Density identity.)} The covariate marginal of \(P_{\mathrm S}\), the law of one observed source record, has density \(f_{\mathrm S}\) with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to \(\mathcal X=[0,1]\). Thus, for every Borel set \(B\subseteq\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{\mathrm S}(X\in B)=\int_{B\cap[0,1]} f_{\mathrm S}(x)\,dx.
\]
\item \textbf{(Pointwise bounds.)} For every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
c_f\le f_{\mathrm S}(x)\le C_f.
\]
\end{itemize}

1cb1f0b6596170079a25bfe98b45885755e6f86b.title: Hölder regularity of the propensity
1cb1f0b6596170079a25bfe98b45885755e6f86b.body:
The source encouragement propensity \(e\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^\beta([0,1],L)\), with Hölder exponent \(\beta=1/8\) and common Hölder radius \(L>1\); explicitly,
\[
\lVert e\rVert_\infty\le L,
\qquad
[e]_\beta\le L.
\]

c4921786b3a1e197c571c853666a9b3ac7737aeb.title: Target density Hölder regularity
c4921786b3a1e197c571c853666a9b3ac7737aeb.body:
The target covariate density \(f_{\mathrm T}\) satisfies the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} The common Hölder radius \(L\) satisfies \(L>1\).
\item \textbf{(Exponent.)} The common Hölder exponent is \(\beta=1/8\).
\item \textbf{(Regularity.)} \(f_{\mathrm T}\in\mathcal H^\beta([0,1],L)\): it is continuous on \([0,1]\) and satisfies
\[
\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|f_{\mathrm T}(x)|\le L,
\qquad
[f_{\mathrm T}]_\beta
=
\sup_{\substack{x,y\in[0,1]\\x\ne y}}
\frac{|f_{\mathrm T}(x)-f_{\mathrm T}(y)|}{|x-y|^\beta}
\le L.
\]
\end{itemize}

aec4a99c64547ddf521be977a2694c0da763476d.title: Outcome consistency and boundedness
aec4a99c64547ddf521be977a2694c0da763476d.body:
In the source population, the observed outcome equals the potential outcome under the realized receipt and lies in the unit interval, both almost surely:
\[
Y=Y(D), \qquad 0\le Y\le 1.
\]

ddd89bb57029a28f78c5bcdf7eb5fb542e136528.title: First-stage strength slice
ddd89bb57029a28f78c5bcdf7eb5fb542e136528.body:
The first-stage strength slice, with \(\mu(P)\) denoting the transported first stage under \(P\), is defined for real parameters \(c_f,C_f,L,a\) and every \(n\in\mathbb N\) by
\[
\mathcal M_n(a)
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal M_n:
0<a\le\frac14,\quad
a\le\mu(P)\le\frac14
\right\}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal M_n\) is the model class of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with parameters \(c_f,C_f,L\).

99dfff611e374421c618d2f509d2acb8cc422b15.title: Hölder regularity of arm means
99dfff611e374421c618d2f509d2acb8cc422b15.body:
The source conditional arm means \(m_{Az}\), for responses \(A\in\{Y,D\}\) and encouragement arms \(z\in\{0,1\}\), satisfy the following conditions, with common Hölder radius \(L\) and Hölder exponent \(\beta\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smoothness.)} \(L>1\), \(\beta=1/8\), and each \(m_{Az}\) is continuous on \([0,1]\), with
\[
\lVert m_{Az}\rVert_\infty\le L,
\qquad
[m_{Az}]_\beta\le L.
\]
\item \textbf{(Range.)} For every \(A\), \(z\), and \(x\in[0,1]\),
\[
0\le m_{Az}(x)\le 1.
\]
\item \textbf{(Source arm moments.)} Under the usual measurability conditions, for every \(A\), \(z\), and measurable set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\),
\[
\int_{\{X\in B,\;Z=z\}} A\,dP_{\mathrm S}
=
\int_B f_{\mathrm S}(x)\,
e(x)^z\bigl(1-e(x)\bigr)^{1-z}\,
m_{Az}(x)\,dx,
\]
where \(P_{\mathrm S}\) is the law of an observed source record, \(f_{\mathrm S}\) is the source covariate density, and \(e\) is the source encouragement propensity.
\end{itemize}

b18fe3db8b3aa42babbbb5e00c8f7174d9706612.title: Marked density vector
b18fe3db8b3aa42babbbb5e00c8f7174d9706612.body:
The marked density vector \(F\), for \(c_f,C_f,L\in\mathbb R\), \(n\in\mathbb N\), and a transport law \(P\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:model-class} with these parameters, is defined for every \(x\in\mathbb R\) by
\[
F(x)=\bigl(f_{\mathrm T}(x),q_0(x),q_1(x),
r_{Y0}(x),r_{Y1}(x),r_{D0}(x),r_{D1}(x)\bigr),
\]
where
\[
q_0(x)=f_{\mathrm S}(x)(1-e(x)),
\qquad
q_1(x)=f_{\mathrm S}(x)e(x),
\qquad
r_{Az}(x)=q_z(x)m_{Az}(x),
\quad A\in\{Y,D\},\quad z\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Here \(f_{\mathrm S}\) and \(f_{\mathrm T}\) are the source and target covariate density carriers, \(e\) is the source encouragement propensity, and \(m_{Az}\) is the source conditional mean of response \(A\) in encouragement arm \(z\). The seven-coordinate index set is
\[
\mathcal I=\{0,1,2,3,4,5,6\},
\]
whose indices correspond, respectively, to \(f_{\mathrm T},q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}\) in the displayed vector.

d8b6b8187bde127c772917f802c26b43b44adc8b.title: Legal instrumental-variable mixture
d8b6b8187bde127c772917f802c26b43b44adc8b.body:
The legal instrumental-variable mixture is the triple consisting of the component law \(Q_{\lambda,\tau}\), the observed-experiment mixture \(M_{\tau}\), and the center law \(P_{\star}\), with parameters satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} The sample size \(n\) is a natural number with
\[
n\ge n_0=256,
\qquad
K_{\mathrm L}=\left\lceil n^{4/3}\right\rceil.
\]
\item \textbf{(Baseline strength.)} The parameter \(a\) satisfies
\[
0<a\le\frac14,
\qquad
b=\bar a=\max\{a,n^{-1/3}\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Amplitude and admissibility.)} The amplitude \(c_{\star}\) satisfies \(c_{\star}<1\) and \(\operatorname{Adm}_{n,a}(c_{\star})\), where
\[
h=h_n=c_{\star}K_{\mathrm L}^{-1/8},
\]
\[
\operatorname{Adm}_{n,a}(c_{\star})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0<c_{\star},\qquad
h\le\frac{3}{16},\qquad
h^2\le b\left(\frac14-h^2\right).
\]
The construction domain also requires \(n>0\).
\item \textbf{(Indices.)} The cellwise sign vector and continuum index satisfy
\[
\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}},
\qquad
\tau\in[-1,1].
\]
\end{itemize}
Write \(u_{\lambda}\) for the tiled covariate perturbation indexed by the cell signs, and set
\[
v_{\lambda,\tau}=\tau u_{\lambda}.
\]
The component \(Q_{\lambda,\tau}\) has source and target covariate densities and encouragement probabilities
\[
f_{\mathrm S}=1,
\qquad
f_{\mathrm T}=1+u_{\lambda},
\qquad
e_1^{(\lambda)}=\frac12+u_{\lambda},
\qquad
e_0^{(\lambda)}=\frac12-u_{\lambda}.
\]
For \(z,d,y\in\{0,1\}\), its source joint cells conditional on \(X=x\) are
\[
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(Z=z,D=d,Y=y\mid X=x)
=
e_z^{(\lambda)}(x)R_z^{(b)}(d,y)
+\frac{v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)(2y-1)}4,
\]
where \(R_z^{(b)}(d,y)\) is the baseline receipt--outcome cell probability at compliance share \(b\). The conditional cells given encouragement and covariates are
\[
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(D=d,Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x)
=
\frac{
e_z^{(\lambda)}(x)R_z^{(b)}(d,y)
+v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)(2y-1)/4
}{
e_z^{(\lambda)}(x)
}.
\]

Let \(C\) denote the complier indicator, \(D(z)\) potential receipt under encouragement \(z\), and \(Y(d)\) the potential outcome under receipt \(d\). The complier outcome margins are
\[
M_{1y}(x)
=
P(C=1,Y(1)=y\mid X=x)
=
\frac b2-
\frac{(2y-1)u_{\lambda}(x)v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)}
{2\{1/4-u_{\lambda}(x)^2\}},
\]
\[
M_{0y}(x)
=
P(C=1,Y(0)=y\mid X=x)
=
\frac b2+
\frac{(2y-1)u_{\lambda}(x)v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)}
{2\{1/4-u_{\lambda}(x)^2\}},
\qquad y\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Always-takers and never-takers receive the conditional masses
\[
P(D(0)=D(1)=1,Y(1)=y\mid X=x)
=
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(D=1,Y=y\mid Z=0,X=x),
\]
\[
P(D(0)=D(1)=0,Y(0)=y\mid X=x)
=
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(D=0,Y=y\mid Z=1,X=x).
\]
For compliers, define
\[
P(Y(d)=y\mid X=x,C=1)
=
\frac{M_{dy}(x)}b,
\qquad d,y\in\{0,1\},
\]
and couple \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently under these binary marginals. Set the unused potential outcomes to
\[
Y(0)=0\quad\text{for always-takers},
\qquad
Y(1)=0\quad\text{for never-takers}.
\]
Draw encouragement according to
\[
Z\ \perp\ (D(0),D(1),Y(0),Y(1))\mid X,
\qquad
P(Z=1\mid X=x)=e_1^{(\lambda)}(x),
\]
and observe
\[
D=D(Z),
\qquad
Y=Y(D).
\]
Use the same conditional primitive full-data law given \(X\) in source and target. Represent the combined law with the convention
\[
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(S=\mathrm{source})
=
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(S=\mathrm{target})
=
\frac12.
\]
This allocation specifies the representation of the constructed witness, and admissibility specifies its construction parameters.

The center law is
\[
P_{\star}
=
\left.Q_{\lambda,\tau}\right|_{u_{\lambda}=v_{\lambda,\tau}=0},
\]
retaining the baseline compliance share \(b\) and the convention
\[
P_{\star}(S=\mathrm{source})
=
P_{\star}(S=\mathrm{target})
=
\frac12.
\]
Write \(P_{\star}^{(n,n)}\) for its observed experiment comprising independent source and target product samples, each of size \(n\).

Finally, \(M_{\tau}\) is the uniform mixture, with weight \(2^{-K_{\mathrm L}}\) for each of the \(2^{K_{\mathrm L}}\) sign vectors, of the observed experiments induced by \(Q_{\lambda,\tau}\), each comprising independent source and target product samples of size \(n\). The defining triple is
\[
\bigl(Q_{\lambda,\tau},\,M_{\tau},\,P_{\star}\bigr).
\]

3553900c8e96a3c02d377f9cb8bd0a0855f44ffd.title: Deterministic sample blocks
3553900c8e96a3c02d377f9cb8bd0a0855f44ffd.body:
The deterministic block \(\mathcal B_b^G\) in sample channel \(G\), for sample size \(n\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\) and block index \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), uses zero-based record indices and is defined by
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
i\in\mathbb Z:
0\le i<n,\quad
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le i<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\}.
\]

b6220ebe24a3f7d9c4b0e1d9cd6dd22af538218d.title: Seven-coordinate marked density vector
b6220ebe24a3f7d9c4b0e1d9cd6dd22af538218d.body:
The marked density vector \(F\), for \(c_f,C_f,L\in\mathbb R\), \(n\in\mathbb N\), and a transport law \(P\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:model-class} with these parameters, is defined for every \(x\in\mathbb R\) by
\[
F(x)=\bigl(f_{\mathrm T}(x),q_0(x),q_1(x),
r_{Y0}(x),r_{Y1}(x),r_{D0}(x),r_{D1}(x)\bigr),
\]
where
\[
q_0(x)=f_{\mathrm S}(x)(1-e(x)),
\qquad
q_1(x)=f_{\mathrm S}(x)e(x),
\qquad
r_{Az}(x)=q_z(x)m_{Az}(x),
\quad A\in\{Y,D\},\quad z\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Here \(f_{\mathrm S}\) and \(f_{\mathrm T}\) are the source and target covariate density carriers, \(e\) is the source encouragement propensity, and \(m_{Az}\) is the source conditional mean of response \(A\) in encouragement arm \(z\).

The coordinate index set is
\[
\mathcal I=\{0,1,2,3,4,5,6\},
\qquad
(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5,F_6)
=(f_{\mathrm T},q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}).
\]
Throughout, the coordinate subscripts of the vector \(F_i\), histogram \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}\), residual \(R_{i,K}^{(b)}\), and observable mark \(W_{i,r}\) use this same numeric indexing: \(i=0,1,2,3,4,5,6\) refers, respectively, to the coordinates \(f_{\mathrm T},q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}\). The channel \(g(0)\) is the target sample channel, and \(g(i)\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}\) is the source sample channel.

5999fccf4ffefca25bae8a505a728852bd5b9b2c.title: Cubic corrected contrast estimator
5999fccf4ffefca25bae8a505a728852bd5b9b2c.body:
The cubic estimator \(\widehat T_A\) is defined for any \(c_f,C_f\in\mathbb R\), sample size \(n\in\mathbb N\), paired samples \((\mathcal S_n,\mathcal T_n)\) containing \(n\) source records and \(n\) target covariates, and response \(A\in\{Y,D\}\), using the functional in \cref{obj:def:smooth-functional}. Set
\[
n_0=256,\qquad \mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\}.
\]
The index \(i\in\mathcal I\) denotes position \(i\), counted from zero, in the seven-coordinate vector of \cref{obj:def:marked-density-vector}. Throughout, \(\widehat F_i\), \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}\), \(R_{i,K}^{(b)}\), \(W_{i,r}\), and \(g(i)\) use that same coordinate position; named-coordinate subscripts in the underlying constructions are read as their corresponding positions in this vector.

Use the blocks, resolutions, histograms, pilot, and residuals of \cref{obj:synth_2,obj:synth_7,obj:synth_14}, with record indices \(r=0,\ldots,n-1\). A one-based block presentation is reindexed by
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\{r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:r+1
\text{ belongs to the one-based block }b\text{ of channel }G\}.
\]
Under this reindexing, \(W_{i,r}\) and \(X_r^{g(i)}\) denote the mark and covariate of record \(r+1\) in the one-based presentation.

For \(n\ge n_0\), write
\[
K_0=K_0(n),\qquad K_2=K_2(n),\qquad K_3=K_3(n),
\qquad
x_{\ell,K}=\frac{\ell-\tfrac12}{K},
\quad \ell=1,\ldots,K.
\]
Define the linear correction by
\[
\mathsf L_A
=
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
\left\{
\frac{1}{m_1}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_1^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\partial_i\Phi_A\bigl(\widehat F(X_r^{g(i)})\bigr)
-
\int_0^1
\partial_i\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\widehat F_i(x)\,dx
\right\},
\]
the quadratic correction by
\[
\mathsf Q_A
=
\frac{1}{2K_2}
\sum_{i,j\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_2}
\partial_{ij}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_2}))
R_{i,K_2}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_2})
R_{j,K_2}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_2}),
\]
and the cubic correction by
\[
\mathsf C_A
=
\frac{1}{6K_3}
\sum_{i,j,k\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_3}
\partial_{ijk}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_3}))
R_{i,K_3}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{j,K_3}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{k,K_3}^{(3)}(x_{\ell,K_3}).
\]
The residual factors retain their displayed block indices even when coordinate indices coincide. The estimator is
\[
\widehat T_A
=
\begin{cases}
0,& n<n_0,\\[2pt]
\displaystyle
\int_0^1\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\,dx
+\mathsf L_A+\mathsf Q_A+\mathsf C_A,
& n\ge n_0.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(n<n_0\), the score interval of \cref{obj:def:score-interval} takes the fallback
\[
I_n=\Theta=[-1,1].
\]

059cca212ac94cd70c8e82e426aadc67de9e63e4.title: Legal IV mixture construction
059cca212ac94cd70c8e82e426aadc67de9e63e4.body:
The legal IV mixture is the triple \((Q_{\lambda,\tau},M_{\tau},P_{\star})\), consisting of a component law, its uniform sign-mixture experiment, and a center law, defined for the following parameters:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\in\mathbb N\) satisfies
\[
n\ge n_0=256,
\qquad
K_{\mathrm L}=\left\lceil n^{4/3}\right\rceil.
\]
Here \(K_{\mathrm L}\) is the number of perturbation cells.
\item \textbf{(Baseline strength.)} The strength parameter \(a\) satisfies \(0<a\le1/4\), and the baseline compliance share is
\[
b=\bar a=\max\{a,n^{-1/3}\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Amplitude and admissibility.)} The amplitude \(c_{\star}\) satisfies \(c_{\star}<1\). With perturbation height
\[
h=h_n=c_{\star}K_{\mathrm L}^{-1/8},
\]
require \(n>0\) and \(\operatorname{Adm}_{n,a}(c_{\star})\), where
\[
\operatorname{Adm}_{n,a}(c_{\star})
\Longleftrightarrow
\left(
0<c_{\star}
\ \text{and}\
h\le\frac{3}{16}
\ \text{and}\
h^2\le b\left(\frac14-h^2\right)
\right).
\]
\item \textbf{(Sign and continuum indices.)} The cellwise sign vector and continuum index satisfy
\[
\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}},
\qquad
\tau\in[-1,1].
\]
For the tiled covariate perturbation \(u_{\lambda}\) indexed by these signs, set
\[
v_{\lambda,\tau}=\tau u_{\lambda}.
\]
\end{itemize}

Define the source and target covariate densities and encouragement probabilities by
\[
f_{\mathrm S}=1,
\qquad
f_{\mathrm T}=1+u_{\lambda},
\qquad
e_1^{(\lambda)}=\frac12+u_{\lambda},
\qquad
e_0^{(\lambda)}=\frac12-u_{\lambda}.
\]
For \(z,d,y\in\{0,1\}\), the source joint cells conditional on covariates are
\[
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(Z=z,D=d,Y=y\mid X=x)
=
e_z^{(\lambda)}(x)R_z^{(b)}(d,y)
+\frac{v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)(2y-1)}4,
\]
where \(R_z^{(b)}(d,y)\) is the baseline receipt–outcome cell probability at compliance share \(b\). The cells conditional on encouragement and covariates are
\[
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(D=d,Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x)
=
\frac{
e_z^{(\lambda)}(x)R_z^{(b)}(d,y)
+v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)(2y-1)/4
}{
e_z^{(\lambda)}(x)
}.
\]

Let \(C\) be the complier indicator, \(D(z)\) potential receipt under encouragement \(z\), and \(Y(d)\) the potential outcome under receipt state \(d\). Define the complier outcome margins by
\[
M_{1y}(x)
=
P(C=1,Y(1)=y\mid X=x)
=
\frac b2
-
\frac{(2y-1)u_{\lambda}(x)v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)}
{2\{1/4-u_{\lambda}(x)^2\}},
\]
\[
M_{0y}(x)
=
P(C=1,Y(0)=y\mid X=x)
=
\frac b2
+
\frac{(2y-1)u_{\lambda}(x)v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)}
{2\{1/4-u_{\lambda}(x)^2\}},
\qquad y\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Assign always-takers and never-takers the conditional masses
\[
P(D(0)=D(1)=1,Y(1)=y\mid X=x)
=
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(D=1,Y=y\mid Z=0,X=x),
\]
\[
P(D(0)=D(1)=0,Y(0)=y\mid X=x)
=
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(D=0,Y=y\mid Z=1,X=x).
\]
For compliers, set \(D(0)=0\), \(D(1)=1\), and
\[
P(Y(d)=y\mid X=x,C=1)
=
\frac{M_{dy}(x)}b,
\qquad d,y\in\{0,1\},
\]
coupling \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently under these binary marginals. Set
\[
Y(0)=0\quad\text{for always-takers},
\qquad
Y(1)=0\quad\text{for never-takers}.
\]
Draw encouragement according to
\[
Z\ \perp\ (D(0),D(1),Y(0),Y(1))\mid X,
\qquad
P(Z=1\mid X=x)=e_1^{(\lambda)}(x),
\]
and observe
\[
D=D(Z),
\qquad
Y=Y(D).
\]
Use the same conditional primitive full-data law given \(X\) in source and target. Represent the resulting combined law \(Q_{\lambda,\tau}\) by
\[
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(S=\mathrm{source})
=
Q_{\lambda,\tau}(S=\mathrm{target})
=
\frac12.
\]
This allocation is a convention for representing the constructed witness; admissibility specifies the parameter domain of the construction.

Define the center law by
\[
P_{\star}
=
\left.Q_{\lambda,\tau}\right|_{u_{\lambda}=v_{\lambda,\tau}=0},
\]
retaining the baseline compliance share \(b\) and the representation convention
\[
P_{\star}(S=\mathrm{source})
=
P_{\star}(S=\mathrm{target})
=
\frac12.
\]
For each component and for the center, take independent source and target product samples, each of size \(n\). Writing \(P_{\mathrm S}\) and \(P_{\mathrm T}\) for the one-record observed source and target laws induced by the law in question, the center experiment and uniform sign mixture are
\[
P_{\star}^{(n,n)}
=
\left.
\left(P_{\mathrm S}^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{\mathrm T}^{\otimes n}\right)
\right|_{P_{\star}},
\]
\[
M_{\tau}
=
2^{-K_{\mathrm L}}
\sum_{\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}}}
\left.
\left(P_{\mathrm S}^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{\mathrm T}^{\otimes n}\right)
\right|_{Q_{\lambda,\tau}}.
\]

fb537ccf01d415f722bba0834c82cb8d3401866c.title: Coordinate indices $\mathcal I$ and sample blocks $\mathcal B_b^G$
fb537ccf01d415f722bba0834c82cb8d3401866c.body:
The coordinate index set is
\[
\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\},
\qquad
(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5,F_6)
=(t,q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}).
\]
For each \(i\in\mathcal I\), its sample channel is
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=0,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus vector, histogram, residual, and mark subscripts use the correspondence
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}
i&0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ \hline
\text{coordinate}&t&q_0&q_1&r_{Y0}&r_{Y1}&r_{D0}&r_{D1}
\end{array}
\]
In particular, for \(V=F\), \(V=H_K^{(b)}\), \(V=R_K^{(b)}\), or \(V=W_r\), named-coordinate subscripts are aliases given by
\[
(V_t,V_{q_0},V_{q_1},V_{r_{Y0}},V_{r_{Y1}},V_{r_{D0}},V_{r_{D1}})
=(V_0,V_1,V_2,V_3,V_4,V_5,V_6).
\]

Write the source records as
\(O_r^{\mathrm S}=(X_r^{\mathrm S},Z_r,D_r,Y_r)\)
and the target records as \(X_r^{\mathrm T}\), for \(r=1,\ldots,n\).
The observable coordinate marks are
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}Y_r,
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}Y_r,\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}D_r,
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}D_r.
\end{aligned}
\]
The mark \(W_{0,r}\) accompanies target record \(r\), and the other marks accompany source record \(r\).

For \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\) and \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), the one-based blocks and their sizes are
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=\{\lfloor bn/4\rfloor+1,\ldots,\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor\},
\qquad
m_b=\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor-\lfloor bn/4\rfloor.
\]
These blocks are the reindexing by \(r=j+1\) of the zero-based blocks:
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
j+1:
j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\},\
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le j<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\}.
\]
Covariates and marks are reindexed together, so a sum in one-based notation satisfies
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in E\}
=
\sum_{\substack{0\le j<n\\
\lfloor bn/4\rfloor\le j<\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor}}
W_{i,j+1}\,\mathbf 1\{X_{j+1}^{g(i)}\in E\}.
\]
Block \(0\) supplies the training records, and blocks \(1,2,3\) supply the evaluation records. Each coordinate-\(i\) sum uses covariates and marks from channel \(g(i)\).

These conventions apply to the objects and conditions in
\cref{obj:synth_1,obj:synth_2,obj:synth_3,obj:synth_4,obj:synth_5,obj:synth_6,obj:synth_7,obj:synth_8,obj:synth_9,obj:synth_10,obj:synth_11,obj:synth_12,obj:synth_13,obj:synth_15,obj:ass:source-iid,obj:ass:target-iid,obj:ass:sample-independence,obj:ass:source-density-bounds,obj:ass:target-density-bounds,obj:ass:source-density-holder,obj:ass:target-density-holder,obj:ass:propensity-overlap,obj:ass:propensity-holder,obj:ass:arm-means-holder,obj:ass:receipt-consistency,obj:ass:outcome-consistency,obj:ass:instrument-randomization,obj:ass:exclusion,obj:ass:monotonicity,obj:ass:transport-complier-outcome,obj:ass:transport-complier-share,obj:ass:positive-strength,obj:def:model-class,obj:def:fixed-geometry-subclass,obj:def:known-geometry-score,obj:def:known-geometry-interval,obj:def:finite-cell-subclass,obj:def:continuous-geometry-witness,obj:def:marked-density-vector,obj:def:smooth-functional,obj:def:cubic-estimator,obj:def:score-interval,obj:def:honest-intervals,obj:def:strength-slice,obj:def:length-frontier,obj:def:legal-iv-mixture,obj:def:unequal-sample-handle,obj:lem:transported-cace-identification,obj:lem:observable-marked-reduction,obj:lem:marked-cubic-mse,obj:oeq:unequal-sample-frontier,obj:lem:random-set-length-identity,obj:lem:legal-iv-mixture-full-elbow,obj:thm:honest-upper-full-elbow,obj:thm:honest-lower-full-elbow,obj:thm:sharp-length-frontier-full-elbow}.

f484eb39676dbf063b7c6c9b3eefb9729d36454c.title: Marked histogram $H_{i,K}^{(b)}$
f484eb39676dbf063b7c6c9b3eefb9729d36454c.body:
The marked histogram is
\[
H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,&n<256,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{K}{m_b}
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K-1}
\mathbf 1\{x\in E_{\ell,K}\}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in E_{\ell,K}\},
&n\ge256,
\end{cases}
\]
for samples \(\mathcal S_n\) and \(\mathcal T_n\) consisting of \(n\) source records and \(n\) target covariates, respectively, coordinate \(i\in\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\}\), resolution \(K\in\{0,1,\ldots\}\), block \(b\in\{0,\ldots,3\}\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\).
For \(K\ge1\) and \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), the cells are
\[
E_{\ell,K}=
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K,(\ell+1)/K),&\ell<K-1,\\
[\ell/K,1],&\ell=K-1.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(K=0\), the sum over cells is empty and equals zero.

The numerical coordinate subscripts correspond to the marked-density vector as follows:
\[
(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5,F_6)
=(t,q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}).
\]
For \(V=F\), \(V=H_K^{(b)}\), \(V=R_K^{(b)}\), or \(V=W_r\), the corresponding named-coordinate subscripts are aliases:
\[
(V_t,V_{q_0},V_{q_1},V_{r_{Y0}},V_{r_{Y1}},V_{r_{D0}},V_{r_{D1}})
=(V_0,V_1,V_2,V_3,V_4,V_5,V_6).
\]

Here records are indexed by \(r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\). For either sample channel \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\), the deterministic block and its size are
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le r<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\},
\qquad
m_b=
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
-
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
The one-based blocks in \cref{obj:synth_14} are obtained by adding one to every record index, with the covariate and mark indices shifted together. The sample channel is
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=0,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus \(X_r^{g(i)}\) is the observed covariate of record \(r\) in the assigned channel.

For source record \(r\), write \(Z_r\) for encouragement, \(Y_r\) for the observed outcome, and \(D_r\) for treatment receipt. The observable marks are
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\},
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The mark \(W_{0,r}\) accompanies target record \(r\), and the other marks accompany source record \(r\).

The histogram uses the objects and conditions in
\cref{obj:synth_1,obj:synth_2,obj:synth_3,obj:synth_4,obj:synth_5,obj:synth_6,obj:synth_8,obj:synth_9,obj:synth_10,obj:synth_11,obj:synth_12,obj:synth_13,obj:synth_15,obj:ass:source-iid,obj:ass:target-iid,obj:ass:sample-independence,obj:ass:source-density-bounds,obj:ass:target-density-bounds,obj:ass:source-density-holder,obj:ass:target-density-holder,obj:ass:propensity-overlap,obj:ass:propensity-holder,obj:ass:arm-means-holder,obj:ass:receipt-consistency,obj:ass:outcome-consistency,obj:ass:instrument-randomization,obj:ass:exclusion,obj:ass:monotonicity,obj:ass:transport-complier-outcome,obj:ass:transport-complier-share,obj:ass:positive-strength,obj:def:model-class,obj:def:fixed-geometry-subclass,obj:def:known-geometry-score,obj:def:known-geometry-interval,obj:def:finite-cell-subclass,obj:def:continuous-geometry-witness,obj:def:marked-density-vector,obj:def:smooth-functional,obj:def:cubic-estimator,obj:def:score-interval,obj:def:honest-intervals,obj:def:strength-slice,obj:def:length-frontier,obj:def:legal-iv-mixture,obj:def:unequal-sample-handle,obj:lem:transported-cace-identification,obj:lem:observable-marked-reduction,obj:lem:marked-cubic-mse,obj:oeq:unequal-sample-frontier,obj:lem:random-set-length-identity,obj:lem:legal-iv-mixture-full-elbow,obj:thm:honest-upper-full-elbow,obj:thm:honest-lower-full-elbow,obj:thm:sharp-length-frontier-full-elbow}.

4a6487b4f9df30fdfba82be3a2b21fe5191b5cea.title: Blockwise marked histogram
4a6487b4f9df30fdfba82be3a2b21fe5191b5cea.body:
The marked histogram is
\[
H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,&n<256,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{K}{m_b}
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K-1}
\mathbf 1\{x\in E_{\ell,K}\}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in E_{\ell,K}\},
&n\ge256,
\end{cases}
\]
for samples \(\mathcal S_n\) and \(\mathcal T_n\) consisting of \(n\) source records and \(n\) target covariates, respectively, where \(n\in\{0,1,\ldots\}\), \(i\in\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\}\), \(K\in\{0,1,\ldots\}\), \(b\in\{0,\ldots,3\}\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\).
For \(K\ge1\), the cells are
\[
E_{\ell,K}=
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K,(\ell+1)/K),&0\le\ell<K-1,\\
[\ell/K,1],&\ell=K-1.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(K=0\), the cell sum is empty and \(H_{i,0}^{(b)}(x)=0\).

Records in both samples are indexed by \(r\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For either sample channel \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\), the deterministic block and its size are
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
r\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor+1
\le r\le
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\},
\qquad
m_b=
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
-
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
This uses the one-based record indexing of \cref{obj:synth_14}, with covariates and marks indexed together. The sample channel is
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=0,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(X_r^{g(i)}\) denotes the observed covariate of record \(r\) in the assigned channel.

For source record \(r\), let \(Z_r\in\{0,1\}\) denote encouragement, \(D_r\in\{0,1\}\) treatment receipt, and \(Y_r\in\mathbb R\) the observed outcome. The observable marks are
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\},
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The mark \(W_{0,r}\) accompanies target record \(r\); the other marks accompany source record \(r\).

The coordinate order agrees with the marked-density vector in \cref{obj:def:marked-density-vector}:
\[
(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5,F_6)
=(t,q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}).
\]
For \(V=F\), \(V=H_K^{(b)}\), \(V=R_K^{(b)}\), or \(V=W_r\), named-coordinate subscripts are aliases:
\[
(V_t,V_{q_0},V_{q_1},V_{r_{Y0}},V_{r_{Y1}},V_{r_{D0}},V_{r_{D1}})
=(V_0,V_1,V_2,V_3,V_4,V_5,V_6).
\]

a1c65723b304a036a3eaa6f28c102aa4e727bbee.title: Cubic corrected functional estimator
a1c65723b304a036a3eaa6f28c102aa4e727bbee.body:
The estimator \(\widehat T_A\) is defined for each response \(A\in\{Y,D\}\), real inputs \(c_f,C_f\), sample size \(n\in\{0,1,\ldots\}\), and observed source and target samples \((\mathcal S_n,\mathcal T_n)\), each containing \(n\) records. Set \(n_0=256\).
