Use zero-based block labels throughout: \(\mathcal B_0^G\) is the pilot block, and \(\mathcal B_1^G,\mathcal B_2^G,\mathcal B_3^G\) are the three evaluation blocks; \(m_b\) denotes the size of block \(b\).

For \(n\ge n_0\), use the supplied resolutions \(K_0=K_0(n)\), \(K_2=K_2(n)\), and \(K_3=K_3(n)\), the clipped pilot \(\widehat F\), and the block-specific residuals \(R_{i,K}^{(b)}\). The coordinate index set \(\mathcal I\) contains the seven marked-density coordinates of \(\cref{obj:def:marked-density-vector}\), and \(\Phi_A\) is the functional integrand of \(\cref{obj:def:smooth-functional}\). Define the cell midpoints by
\[
x_{\ell,K}=\frac{\ell-\tfrac12}{K},
\qquad \ell=1,\ldots,K.
\]
The linear, quadratic, and cubic corrections are
\[
\mathsf L_A=
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
\left\{
\frac{1}{m_1}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_1^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\partial_i\Phi_A\bigl(\widehat F(X_r^{g(i)})\bigr)
-
\int_0^1
\partial_i\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\widehat F_i(x)\,dx
\right\},
\]
\[
\mathsf Q_A=
\frac{1}{2K_2}
\sum_{i,j\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_2}
\partial_{ij}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_2}))
R_{i,K_2}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_2})
R_{j,K_2}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_2}),
\]
and
\[
\mathsf C_A=
\frac{1}{6K_3}
\sum_{i,j,k\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_3}
\partial_{ijk}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_3}))
R_{i,K_3}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{j,K_3}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{k,K_3}^{(3)}(x_{\ell,K_3}).
\]
Here \(g(i)\) selects the source or target channel for coordinate \(i\), \(W_{i,r}\) is its observable mark, and \(X_r^{g(i)}\) is the corresponding observed covariate. Repeated coordinate indices retain the distinct evaluation blocks displayed in the products.

The estimator is
\[
\widehat T_A=
\begin{cases}
0,& n<n_0,\\[2pt]
\displaystyle
\int_0^1\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\,dx+
\mathsf L_A+\mathsf Q_A+\mathsf C_A,
& n\ge n_0.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(n<n_0\), the score interval of \(\cref{obj:def:score-interval}\) takes the fallback value
\[
I_n=\Theta=[-1,1].
\]

9201c2e483e3cabc7f122cb86c5e87726e4219ac.title: Coordinate indices and sample blocks
9201c2e483e3cabc7f122cb86c5e87726e4219ac.body:
The coordinate index set is
\[
\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\},
\qquad
(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5,F_6)
=(t,q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}).
\]
For each \(i\in\mathcal I\), its sample channel is
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=0,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Vector, histogram, residual, and mark subscripts use the correspondence
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}
i&0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ \hline
\text{coordinate}&t&q_0&q_1&r_{Y0}&r_{Y1}&r_{D0}&r_{D1}
\end{array}
\]
In particular, for \(V=F\), \(V=H_K^{(b)}\), \(V=R_K^{(b)}\), or \(V=W_r\), named-coordinate subscripts are aliases given by
\[
(V_t,V_{q_0},V_{q_1},V_{r_{Y0}},V_{r_{Y1}},V_{r_{D0}},V_{r_{D1}})
=(V_0,V_1,V_2,V_3,V_4,V_5,V_6).
\]

Write the source records as
\(O_r^{\mathrm S}=(X_r^{\mathrm S},Z_r,D_r,Y_r)\)
and the target records as \(X_r^{\mathrm T}\), for \(r=1,\ldots,n\).
The observable coordinate marks are
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}Y_r,
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}Y_r,\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}D_r,
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}D_r.
\end{aligned}
\]
The mark \(W_{0,r}\) accompanies target record \(r\), and the other marks accompany source record \(r\).

For \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\) and \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), denote the one-based blocks by \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_b^G\), with sizes \(m_b\):
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal B}_b^G
=\{\lfloor bn/4\rfloor+1,\ldots,\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor\},
\qquad
m_b=\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor-\lfloor bn/4\rfloor.
\]
The notation \(\mathcal B_b^G\) denotes the zero-based blocks, and the two conventions are related by
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le j<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\},
\qquad
\widetilde{\mathcal B}_b^G
=\{j+1:j\in\mathcal B_b^G\}.
\]
Covariates and marks are reindexed together, so a sum in one-based notation satisfies
\[
\sum_{r\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in E\}
=
\sum_{\substack{0\le j<n\\
\lfloor bn/4\rfloor\le j<\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor}}
W_{i,j+1}\,\mathbf 1\{X_{j+1}^{g(i)}\in E\}.
\]
Block \(0\) supplies the training records, and blocks \(1,2,3\) supply the evaluation records. Each coordinate-\(i\) sum uses covariates and marks from channel \(g(i)\).

These conventions apply to the objects and conditions in
\cref{obj:synth_1,obj:synth_2,obj:synth_3,obj:synth_4,obj:synth_5,obj:synth_6,obj:synth_7,obj:synth_8,obj:synth_9,obj:synth_10,obj:synth_11,obj:synth_12,obj:synth_13,obj:synth_15,obj:synth_16,obj:synth_17,obj:ass:source-iid,obj:ass:target-iid,obj:ass:sample-independence,obj:ass:source-density-bounds,obj:ass:target-density-bounds,obj:ass:source-density-holder,obj:ass:target-density-holder,obj:ass:propensity-overlap,obj:ass:propensity-holder,obj:ass:arm-means-holder,obj:ass:receipt-consistency,obj:ass:outcome-consistency,obj:ass:instrument-randomization,obj:ass:exclusion,obj:ass:monotonicity,obj:ass:transport-complier-outcome,obj:ass:transport-complier-share,obj:ass:positive-strength,obj:def:model-class,obj:def:fixed-geometry-subclass,obj:def:known-geometry-score,obj:def:known-geometry-interval,obj:def:finite-cell-subclass,obj:def:continuous-geometry-witness,obj:def:marked-density-vector,obj:def:smooth-functional,obj:def:cubic-estimator,obj:def:score-interval,obj:def:honest-intervals,obj:def:strength-slice,obj:def:length-frontier,obj:def:legal-iv-mixture,obj:def:unequal-sample-handle,obj:lem:transported-cace-identification,obj:lem:observable-marked-reduction,obj:lem:marked-cubic-mse,obj:oeq:unequal-sample-frontier,obj:lem:random-set-length-identity,obj:lem:legal-iv-mixture-full-elbow,obj:thm:honest-upper-full-elbow,obj:thm:honest-lower-full-elbow,obj:thm:sharp-length-frontier-full-elbow}.

f661eded286cfdba5fac23a28fbd856d3aadc804.title: Marked histogram residual
f661eded286cfdba5fac23a28fbd856d3aadc804.body:
The residual \(R_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)\) is defined by
\[
R_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)
=
H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)-\widehat F_i(x),
\]
where the marked histogram \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}\) and the clipped pilot vector \(\widehat F\) are defined in \cref{obj:synth_7,obj:synth_8}, respectively. The parameters are arbitrary nonnegative integers \(n\) and \(K\), data consisting of \(n\) source records and \(n\) target covariates, a coordinate index \(i\) among the seven coordinates, a block index \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), an evaluation point \(x\in\mathbb R\), and pilot-clipping parameters \(c_f,C_f\in\mathbb R\).

6d7960d5f994ddcc675ecf277b72fddd81f1fce8.title: Clipped marked-density pilot vector
6d7960d5f994ddcc675ecf277b72fddd81f1fce8.body:
The pilot vector \(\widehat F(x)\), with coordinates indexed by \(i\in\{0,\ldots,6\}\), is defined for real envelope parameters \(c_f,C_f\), a sample-size index \(n\in\mathbb N\), source and target samples \((\mathcal S_n,\mathcal T_n)\) each of size \(n\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\). For \(n<256\), set
\[
\widehat F(x)=\left(1,\frac12,\frac12,0,0,0,0\right).
\]
For \(n\ge256\), let \(K_0(n)\) be the dyadic pilot resolution with exponent \(4/5\), and form the block-\(0\) marked histogram
\[
H_{i,K_0(n)}^{(0)}(x)
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K_0(n)-1}
\mathbf 1\{x\in\text{cell }\ell\}
\frac{K_0(n)}{m_0}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_0^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in\text{cell }\ell\}.
\]
Here the cells are those of the resolution-\(K_0(n)\) partition, \(m_0\) is the size of block \(0\), and the sample-channel selector \(g(i)\), observable marks \(W_{i,r}\), covariates \(X_r^{g(i)}\), and blocks \(\mathcal B_0^{g(i)}\) use the definitions and zero-based record indexing of \(\cref{obj:synth_14}\). Define \(\widehat F_i(x)\) by clipping \(H_{i,K_0(n)}^{(0)}(x)\) with the following lower and upper cutoffs, respectively:
\[
\begin{cases}
(c_f,C_f), & i=0,\\
(c_f/4,3C_f/4), & i\in\{1,2\},\\
(0,3C_f/4), & i\in\{3,4,5,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]

a77ab4442638fce1b3ed1bde6e56b733f932b40c.title: Blockwise marked histogram
a77ab4442638fce1b3ed1bde6e56b733f932b40c.body:
The marked histogram \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)\), for coordinate \(i\), resolution \(K\), block \(b\), and evaluation point \(x\), is defined by
\[
H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,&n<256,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{K}{m_b}
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K-1}
\mathbf 1\{x\in E_{\ell,K}\}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in E_{\ell,K}\},
&n\ge256.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\mathcal S_n\), the source sample, and \(\mathcal T_n\), the target covariate sample, each contain \(n\) records, with
\[
n,K\in\{0,1,\ldots\},\qquad
i\in\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\},\qquad
b\in\{0,\ldots,3\},\qquad
x\in\mathbb R.
\]
For \(K\ge1\), the cells \(E_{\ell,K}\) are
\[
E_{\ell,K}=
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K,(\ell+1)/K),&0\le\ell<K-1,\\
[\ell/K,1],&\ell=K-1.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(K=0\), the cell sum is empty and \(H_{i,0}^{(b)}(x)=0\).

Using zero-based record indices \(r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), with an empty index set when \(n=0\), the deterministic block \(\mathcal B_b^G\) for sample channel \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\) and its size \(m_b\) are
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le r<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\},
\qquad
m_b=
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
-
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
The assigned sample channel \(g(i)\) is
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=0,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]
The covariate \(X_r^{g(i)}\) is the observed covariate of zero-based record \(r\) in that channel.

For source record \(r\), let \(Z_r\in\{0,1\}\) denote encouragement, \(D_r\in\{0,1\}\) treatment receipt, and \(Y_r\in\mathbb R\) the observed outcome. The observable marks \(W_{i,r}\), indexed together with their covariates, are defined by
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\},
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The constant mark \(W_{0,r}\) accompanies target record \(r\); the remaining marks accompany source record \(r\).

d06bc7c2333575388482d584de3b0fc721da2ec3.title: Split-block cubic estimator
d06bc7c2333575388482d584de3b0fc721da2ec3.body:
The cubic estimator \(\widehat T_A\) is defined for \(c_f,C_f\in\mathbb R\), a sample size \(n\in\mathbb N\), two observed samples \((\mathcal S_n,\mathcal T_n)\) of size \(n\) each, and \(A\in\{Y,D\}\). Set \(n_0=256\). Use the deterministic blocks, normalized marked histograms, clipped pilot, residuals, coordinate channels, and observable marks defined in \cref{obj:synth_14}. In particular, record indices are zero-based, and every \(W_{i,r}\) has exactly the mark definition in \cref{obj:synth_14}.

For \(n\ge n_0\), write
\[
K_0=K_0(n),\qquad K_2=K_2(n),\qquad K_3=K_3(n),
\qquad
x_{\ell,K}=\frac{\ell-\tfrac12}{K},
\quad \ell=1,\ldots,K.
\]
With the seven-coordinate index set \(\mathcal I\) and the functional integrand \(\Phi_A\) of \cref{obj:def:smooth-functional}, define
\[
\mathsf L_A=
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
\left\{
\frac{1}{m_1}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_1^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\partial_i\Phi_A\bigl(\widehat F(X_r^{g(i)})\bigr)
-
\int_0^1
\partial_i\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\widehat F_i(x)\,dx
\right\},
\]
where the record sum uses the zero-based block convention of \cref{obj:synth_14}. Define the quadratic and cubic corrections by
\[
\mathsf Q_A=
\frac{1}{2K_2}
\sum_{i,j\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_2}
\partial_{ij}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_2}))
R_{i,K_2}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_2})
R_{j,K_2}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_2})
\]
and
\[
\mathsf C_A=
\frac{1}{6K_3}
\sum_{i,j,k\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_3}
\partial_{ijk}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_3}))
R_{i,K_3}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{j,K_3}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{k,K_3}^{(3)}(x_{\ell,K_3}).
\]
These formulas use evaluation blocks \(1,2\) for the two quadratic factors and \(1,2,3\) for the three cubic factors, including when coordinate indices coincide. Set
\[
\widehat T_A=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\int_0^1\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\,dx+
\mathsf L_A+\mathsf Q_A+\mathsf C_A,
& n\ge n_0,\\
0,& n<n_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The dyadic resolutions satisfy \(K_0\mid K_3\) and \(K_3\mid K_2\). Each pilot-composition integral above admits the exact cell-sum representation
\[
\int_0^1 g(\widehat F(x))\,dx
=
\frac{1}{K}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K}
g(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K})),
\qquad K>0,\quad K_0\mid K,
\]
for any real-valued function \(g\) of the density vector. For \(n<n_0\), the interval in \cref{obj:def:score-interval} takes the fallback \(I_n=\Theta=[-1,1]\).

90921d800a898b172a0d23b64f79b7882e037dc5.title: Split-block cubic estimator
90921d800a898b172a0d23b64f79b7882e037dc5.body:
The cubic estimator \(\widehat T_A\) is defined for arbitrary \(c_f,C_f\in\mathbb R\), a sample size \(n\in\mathbb N\), two observed samples \((\mathcal S_n,\mathcal T_n)\) of size \(n\) each, and response \(A\in\{Y,D\}\). Set \(n_0=256\). Use the deterministic blocks, normalized marked histograms, clipped pilot, residuals, coordinate channels, and observable marks of \cref{obj:synth_14}, with its zero-based record indices.

Each derivative operator takes the value zero where its defining differentiability condition fails. For \(n\ge n_0\), write
\[
K_0=K_0(n),\qquad K_2=K_2(n),\qquad K_3=K_3(n),
\qquad

\quad \ell=1,\ldots,K.
\]
With the seven-coordinate index set \(\mathcal I\) of \cref{obj:synth_14} and the functional integrand \(\Phi_A\) of \cref{obj:def:smooth-functional}, define
\[
\mathsf L_A=
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
\left\{
\frac{1}{m_1}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_1^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\partial_i\Phi_A\bigl(\widehat F(X_r^{g(i)})\bigr)
-
\int_0^1
\partial_i\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\widehat F_i(x)\,dx
\right\},
\]
\[
\mathsf Q_A=
\frac{1}{2K_2}
\sum_{i,j\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_2}
\partial_{ij}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_2}))
R_{i,K_2}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_2})
R_{j,K_2}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_2}),
\]
and
\[
\mathsf C_A=
\frac{1}{6K_3}
\sum_{i,j,k\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_3}
\partial_{ijk}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_3}))
R_{i,K_3}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{j,K_3}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{k,K_3}^{(3)}(x_{\ell,K_3}).
\]
The quadratic factors use evaluation blocks \(1,2\), and the cubic factors use evaluation blocks \(1,2,3\), including when coordinate indices coincide. Set
\[
\widehat T_A=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle

\mathsf L_A+\mathsf Q_A+\mathsf C_A,

\end{cases}
\]

\[
\int_0^1 g(\widehat F(x))\,dx
=
\frac{1}{K}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K}
g(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K})).
\]
For \(n<n_0\), the interval of \cref{obj:def:score-interval} takes the fallback \(I_n=\Theta=[-1,1]\).

08848de5fc249510a601b230c3fdfebe1e310c70.title: Clipped marked-density pilot vector
08848de5fc249510a601b230c3fdfebe1e310c70.body:
The pilot vector \(\widehat F(x)\), indexed by \(i\in\{0,\ldots,6\}\), is defined for real envelope parameters \(c_f,C_f\), a sample-size index \(n\in\mathbb N\), source and target samples \((\mathcal S_n,\mathcal T_n)\) each of size \(n\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\). For \(n<256\), set
\[
\widehat F(x)=\left(1,\frac12,\frac12,0,0,0,0\right).
\]
For \(n\ge256\), use \(K_0(n)\), the dyadic pilot resolution with exponent \(4/5\), and the block-\(0\) marked histogram \(H_{i,K_0(n)}^{(0)}(x)\) of \cref{obj:synth_7}, with the observable marks and zero-based record indexing of \cref{obj:synth_14}. Define \(\widehat F_i(x)\) by clipping this histogram value with the following lower and upper cutoffs, respectively:
\[
\begin{cases}
(c_f,C_f), & i=0,\\
(c_f/4,3C_f/4), & i\in\{1,2\},\\
(0,3C_f/4), & i\in\{3,4,5,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]

1566e5ba2b96068d9aa9e3ca0bf03e23e130c7fc.title: Blockwise marked histogram definition
1566e5ba2b96068d9aa9e3ca0bf03e23e130c7fc.body:
The marked histogram \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)\), for coordinate \(i\), resolution \(K\), block \(b\), and evaluation point \(x\), is defined by
\[
H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,&n<256,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{K}{m_b}
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K-1}
\mathbf 1\{x\in E_{\ell,K}\}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in E_{\ell,K}\},
&n\ge256.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\mathcal S_n\), the sample of source records, and \(\mathcal T_n\), the sample of target covariates, each contain \(n\) records, and the parameters range over
\[
n,K\in\{0,1,\ldots\},\qquad
i\in\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\},\qquad
b\in\{0,\ldots,3\},\qquad
x\in\mathbb R.
\]
For \(K\ge1\), the cells \(E_{\ell,K}\) are
\[
E_{\ell,K}=
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K,(\ell+1)/K),&0\le\ell<K-1,\\
[\ell/K,1],&\ell=K-1.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(K=0\), the cell sum is empty and \(H_{i,0}^{(b)}(x)=0\).

Both samples use zero-based record indices \(r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), with an empty index set when \(n=0\). For sample channel \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\), the deterministic block \(\mathcal B_b^G\) and its size \(m_b\) are
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le r<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\},
\qquad
m_b=
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
-
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
The sample channel \(g(i)\) assigned to coordinate \(i\) is
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=0,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]
The covariate \(X_r^{g(i)}\) is the observed covariate of zero-based record \(r\) in that channel.

For zero-based source record \(r\), let \(Z_r\in\{0,1\}\) denote encouragement, \(D_r\in\{0,1\}\) treatment receipt, and \(Y_r\in\mathbb R\) the observed outcome. The observable marks \(W_{i,r}\) are
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\},
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The constant mark \(W_{0,r}\) accompanies zero-based target record \(r\); each remaining mark accompanies zero-based source record \(r\). In every block sum, the mark and covariate use the same record index.

da46eb6c39002cd0fb344f54c81dee2b8b4d6900.title: Observable cubic estimator
da46eb6c39002cd0fb344f54c81dee2b8b4d6900.body:
The cubic estimator \(\widehat T_A\) is defined for arbitrary \(c_f,C_f\in\mathbb R\), sample size \(n\in\mathbb N\), observed source and target samples \((\mathcal S_n,\mathcal T_n)\) of size \(n\) each, and response \(A\in\{Y,D\}\). Set
\[
n_0=256.
\]
Use the deterministic blocks, dyadic resolutions, normalized marked histograms, clipped pilot \(\widehat F\), and residuals of \cref{obj:synth_14}, with zero-based record indices \(r=0,\ldots,n-1\). The seven coordinates are indexed by \(\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\}\); coordinate \(0\) uses the target channel and the remaining coordinates use the source channel. For each record index \(r\), the observable marks used in both the histograms and the corrections are
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}D_r,
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}D_r.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(Z_r,D_r,Y_r\) are the encouragement, receipt, and outcome in source record \(r\). Every block sum uses the mark and covariate of that same zero-based record.

Division is totalized by assigning zero to division by zero. The symbols \(\partial_i\Phi_A\), \(\partial_{ij}\Phi_A\), and \(\partial_{ijk}\Phi_A\) denote coordinate evaluations of the corresponding iterated Fréchet derivatives, with each derivative operator assigned zero where its defining differentiability condition fails.

For \(n\ge n_0\), write
\[
K_0=K_0(n),\qquad K_2=K_2(n),\qquad K_3=K_3(n),
\qquad
x_{\ell,K}=\frac{\ell-\tfrac12}{K},
\quad \ell=1,\ldots,K.
\]
Using the functional integrand \(\Phi_A\) of \cref{obj:def:smooth-functional}, define
\[
\mathsf L_A=
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
\left\{
\frac{1}{m_1}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_1^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\partial_i\Phi_A\bigl(\widehat F(X_r^{g(i)})\bigr)
-
\int_0^1
\partial_i\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\widehat F_i(x)\,dx
\right\},
\]
\[
\mathsf Q_A=
\frac{1}{2K_2}
\sum_{i,j\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_2}
\partial_{ij}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_2}))
R_{i,K_2}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_2})
R_{j,K_2}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_2}),
\]
and
\[
\mathsf C_A=
\frac{1}{6K_3}
\sum_{i,j,k\in\mathcal I}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_3}
\partial_{ijk}\Phi_A(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K_3}))
R_{i,K_3}^{(1)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{j,K_3}^{(2)}(x_{\ell,K_3})
R_{k,K_3}^{(3)}(x_{\ell,K_3}).
\]
The quadratic factors use evaluation blocks \(1,2\), and the cubic factors use evaluation blocks \(1,2,3\), including when coordinate indices coincide. Set
\[
\widehat T_A=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\int_0^1\Phi_A(\widehat F(x))\,dx+
\mathsf L_A+\mathsf Q_A+\mathsf C_A,
& n\ge n_0,\\
0,& n<n_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The dyadic resolutions satisfy \(K_0\mid K_3\) and \(K_3\mid K_2\). For every positive integer \(K\) with \(K_0\mid K\) and every real-valued function \(g\) of the density vector,
\[
\int_0^1 g(\widehat F(x))\,dx
=
\frac{1}{K}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K}
g(\widehat F(x_{\ell,K})).
\]
For \(n<n_0\), the interval of \cref{obj:def:score-interval} takes the fallback
\[
I_n=\Theta=[-1,1].
\]

4fc57e7423b520a9238bdca593508e333e4d4a53.title: Coordinate marks \(W_{i,r}\) and sample blocks \(\mathcal B_b^G\)
4fc57e7423b520a9238bdca593508e333e4d4a53.body:
The coordinate index set and coordinate ordering are
\[
\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\},
\qquad
(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5,F_6)
=(t,q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}).
\]
The sample channel of coordinate \(i\in\mathcal I\) is
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=0,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Vector, histogram, residual, and mark subscripts follow the correspondence
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}
i&0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ \hline
\text{coordinate}&t&q_0&q_1&r_{Y0}&r_{Y1}&r_{D0}&r_{D1}.
\end{array}
\]
For \(V=F\), \(V=H_K^{(b)}\), \(V=R_K^{(b)}\), or \(V=W_r\), the named-coordinate subscripts satisfy
\[
(V_t,V_{q_0},V_{q_1},V_{r_{Y0}},V_{r_{Y1}},V_{r_{D0}},V_{r_{D1}})
=(V_0,V_1,V_2,V_3,V_4,V_5,V_6).
\]

Index the source records and target covariate records from zero:
\[
O_r^{\mathrm S}=(X_r^{\mathrm S},Z_r,D_r,Y_r),
\qquad
X_r^{\mathrm T},
\qquad r=0,\ldots,n-1.
\]
Let \(Y_r^{\mathrm{clip}}\) denote the clipped observable outcome used in
\cref{obj:synth_7,obj:synth_8,obj:def:cubic-estimator}.
The observable coordinate marks, with this same clipping convention throughout, are
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}Y_r^{\mathrm{clip}},
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}Y_r^{\mathrm{clip}},\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}D_r,
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}D_r.
\end{aligned}
\]
The mark \(W_{0,r}\) accompanies target record \(r\); the remaining marks accompany source record \(r\).

For \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\) and \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), the blocks and their sizes are
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le r<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\},
\qquad
m_b=\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
-\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
Their one-based counterparts are
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal B}_b^G
=\{r+1:r\in\mathcal B_b^G\}
=\{\lfloor bn/4\rfloor+1,\ldots,\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor\}.
\]
One-based covariates and marks are defined together by
\[
\widetilde X_s^G=X_{s-1}^G,
\qquad
\widetilde W_{i,s}=W_{i,s-1},
\qquad s=1,\ldots,n.
\]
Thus, for a covariate set \(E\), the corresponding block sums satisfy
\[
\sum_{s\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_b^{g(i)}}
\widetilde W_{i,s}\,
\mathbf 1\{\widetilde X_s^{g(i)}\in E\}
=
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in E\}.
\]
Block \(0\) supplies the training records, and blocks \(1,2,3\) supply the evaluation records. Each coordinate-\(i\) sum uses covariates and marks with the same record index in channel \(g(i)\).

These conventions apply to the objects and conditions in
\cref{obj:synth_1,obj:synth_2,obj:synth_3,obj:synth_4,obj:synth_5,obj:synth_6,obj:synth_7,obj:synth_8,obj:synth_9,obj:synth_10,obj:synth_11,obj:synth_12,obj:synth_13,obj:synth_15,obj:synth_16,obj:synth_17,obj:synth_18,obj:ass:source-iid,obj:ass:target-iid,obj:ass:sample-independence,obj:ass:source-density-bounds,obj:ass:target-density-bounds,obj:ass:source-density-holder,obj:ass:target-density-holder,obj:ass:propensity-overlap,obj:ass:propensity-holder,obj:ass:arm-means-holder,obj:ass:receipt-consistency,obj:ass:outcome-consistency,obj:ass:instrument-randomization,obj:ass:exclusion,obj:ass:monotonicity,obj:ass:transport-complier-outcome,obj:ass:transport-complier-share,obj:ass:positive-strength,obj:def:model-class,obj:def:fixed-geometry-subclass,obj:def:known-geometry-score,obj:def:known-geometry-interval,obj:def:finite-cell-subclass,obj:def:continuous-geometry-witness,obj:def:marked-density-vector,obj:def:smooth-functional,obj:def:cubic-estimator,obj:def:score-interval,obj:def:honest-intervals,obj:def:strength-slice,obj:def:length-frontier,obj:def:legal-iv-mixture,obj:def:unequal-sample-handle,obj:lem:transported-cace-identification,obj:lem:observable-marked-reduction,obj:lem:marked-cubic-mse,obj:oeq:unequal-sample-frontier,obj:lem:random-set-length-identity,obj:lem:legal-iv-mixture-full-elbow,obj:thm:honest-upper-full-elbow,obj:thm:honest-lower-full-elbow,obj:thm:sharp-length-frontier-full-elbow}.

02fefb02ce8d2b2dc1f2c849d0d930a5a6ae925a.title: Tiled and coupled perturbations
02fefb02ce8d2b2dc1f2c849d0d930a5a6ae925a.body:
The tiled perturbation \(u_{\lambda}\), for \(c_{\star}\in\mathbb R\), \(n\in\mathbb N\), and a cellwise sign vector \(\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}}\), is defined for every \(x\in\mathbb R\) by
\[
K_{\mathrm L}=\left\lceil n^{4/3}\right\rceil,
\qquad
h_n=c_{\star}K_{\mathrm L}^{-1/8},
\qquad
u_{\lambda}(x)=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K_{\mathrm L}-1}
\begin{cases}
h_n\lambda_\ell\sin\!\bigl(2\pi(K_{\mathrm L}x-\ell)\bigr),
& x\in\operatorname{cell}(K_{\mathrm L},\ell),\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Each sign \(\lambda_\ell\) equals \(1\) when the supplied Boolean entry for cell \(\ell\) is true and \(-1\) when it is false. For \(0\leq\ell<K_{\mathrm L}\), the cells are
\[
\operatorname{cell}(K_{\mathrm L},\ell)=
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K_{\mathrm L},1],
& \ell+1=K_{\mathrm L},\\
[\ell/K_{\mathrm L},(\ell+1)/K_{\mathrm L}),
& \ell+1\ne K_{\mathrm L}.
\end{cases}
\]
At \(n=0\), the sum is empty and equals zero, with the convention \(0^{-1/8}=0\).
The coupled perturbation \(v_{\lambda,\tau}\), for any \(\tau\in\mathbb R\), is defined by
\[
v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)=\tau u_{\lambda}(x),
\qquad x\in\mathbb R.
\]

groups.title: Sample channels and observable coordinate marks
groups.body:
Let
\[
\mathcal I=\{t,q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}\}.
\]
For each coordinate \(i\in\mathcal I\), define its sample channel by
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=t,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\mathcal I\setminus\{t\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Write the source records as
\(O_r^{\mathrm S}=(X_r^{\mathrm S},Z_r,D_r,Y_r)\)
and the target records as \(X_r^{\mathrm T}\), for \(r=1,\ldots,n\).
Thus \(X_r^{g(i)}\) is the covariate of record \(r\) in the channel assigned to coordinate \(i\).
Define the observable coordinate marks by
\[
W_{t,r}=1,\qquad
W_{q_z,r}=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=z\},\qquad
W_{r_{Az},r}=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=z\}A_r,
\quad A\in\{Y,D\},\quad z\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The mark \(W_{t,r}\) accompanies target record \(r\), and every other mark accompanies source record \(r\). For \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\) and \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), records retain their original sample indices within the deterministic blocks
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=\{\lfloor bn/4\rfloor+1,\ldots,\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor\},
\qquad
m_b=\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor-\lfloor bn/4\rfloor.
\]
Block \(0\) supplies the training records, and blocks \(1,2,3\) supply the evaluation records. A coordinate-\(i\) sum over block \(b\) therefore uses the pairs
\((X_r^{g(i)},W_{i,r})\) indexed by \(r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}\).

groups.title: Baseline receipt–outcome cell laws
groups.body:
For a baseline compliance share \(b\in(0,1/4]\) and \(z\in\{0,1\}\), set
\[
r_z^{(b)}=\frac{1+(2z-1)b}{2}.
\]
Define the baseline conditional receipt–outcome probability mass function on \(\{0,1\}^2\) by
\[
R_z^{(b)}(d,y)=
\begin{cases}
r_z^{(b)}/2,&d=1,\\
(1-r_z^{(b)})/2,&d=0,
\end{cases}
\qquad z,d,y\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Equivalently, for each \(y\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
R_0^{(b)}(0,y)=R_1^{(b)}(1,y)=\frac{1+b}{4},
\qquad
R_0^{(b)}(1,y)=R_1^{(b)}(0,y)=\frac{1-b}{4}.
\]
Under this baseline law, receipt has probability \(r_z^{(b)}\) conditional on instrument value \(z\), and the binary outcome is independent of receipt with probability \(1/2\) for each outcome value. In the lower-mixture construction, the baseline share is \(b=\max\{a,n^{-1/3}\}\) for \(n\ge n_0=256\) and \(0<a\le1/4\).

groups.title: Tiled perturbation bump
groups.body:
Define \(\operatorname{bump}:\mathbb R\to[-1,1]\) by
\[
\operatorname{bump}(t)=
\begin{cases}
\sin(2\pi t),&t\in[0,1],\\
0,&t\notin[0,1].
\end{cases}
\]
Its restriction to \([0,1]\) is the function \(B(t)=\sin(2\pi t)\) used in the tiled perturbation. Its support is \([0,1]\), and its normalization is
\[
\|\operatorname{bump}\|_\infty=1,\qquad
\int_0^1\operatorname{bump}(t)\,dt=0,\qquad
\int_0^1\operatorname{bump}(t)^2\,dt=\frac12.
\]
It satisfies \(\operatorname{bump}(1-t)=-\operatorname{bump}(t)\) for \(t\in[0,1]\) and vanishes at both endpoints. The zero extension is continuous and globally Lipschitz with constant \(2\pi\); its restriction to \([0,1]\) is smooth. In particular, for \(\beta=1/8\),
\[
|\operatorname{bump}(s)-\operatorname{bump}(t)|
\le 2\pi |s-t|^\beta,\qquad s,t\in\mathbb R.
\]

groups.title: Distances between observed experiments
groups.body:
For probability measures \(P\) and \(Q\) on the same measurable observation space \((\Omega,\mathcal F)\), define the chi-square divergence by
\[
\chi^2(P,Q)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\int_\Omega
\left(\frac{dP}{dQ}-1\right)^2\,dQ,&P\ll Q,\\
+\infty,&P\not\ll Q.
\end{cases}
\]
The integral is understood in the extended nonnegative reals. Define total-variation distance with the probability-distance normalization by
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)
=\sup_{A\in\mathcal F}|P(A)-Q(A)|
=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left|\frac{dP}{d\nu}-\frac{dQ}{d\nu}\right|\,d\nu,
\qquad \nu=P+Q.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)\in[0,1]\). For the lower mixture, take \(P=M_\tau\) and \(Q=P_\star^{(n,n)}\) on the observation space of the independent source and target samples, each of size \(n\).

groups.title: Resolution-\(K\) interval cells
groups.body:
For a positive integer \(K\) and an index \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), define
\[
\operatorname{cell}(K,\ell)=
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K,(\ell+1)/K),&0\le\ell<K-1,\\
[(K-1)/K,1],&\ell=K-1.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus each cell includes its left endpoint, and the final cell also includes the endpoint \(1\).

groups.title: Target-density coordinate
groups.body:
In the marked-density vector, \(t\) denotes the target covariate density:
\[
t:=f_{\mathrm T},\qquad t(x)=f_{\mathrm T}(x),\quad x\in[0,1].
\]
Thus \(F_0=t=f_{\mathrm T}\), and the named-coordinate subscript \(t\) denotes coordinate \(0\): \(V_t:=V_0\) for \(V=F\), \(V=H_K^{(b)}\), \(V=R_K^{(b)}\), or \(V=W_r\). In particular, \(F_t=f_{\mathrm T}\). In \(\operatorname{bump}(t)\) and \(\int_{\Theta}P(t\in C_n)\,dt\), \(t\) is instead a local real argument or integration variable, respectively.

synth_1.title: The scalar covariate space
synth_1.body:
The covariate space is
\[
\mathcal X := [0,1] \subset \mathbb R.
\]

synth_2.title: Deterministic sample blocks
synth_2.body:
The deterministic block \(\mathcal B_b^G\) in sample channel \(G\), for sample size \(n\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\) and block index \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), uses zero-based record indices and is defined by
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
i\in\mathbb Z:
0\le i<n,\quad
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le i<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\}.
\]

synth_3.title: Exact block size
synth_3.body:
The block size \(m_b\), for a nonnegative integer \(n\) and an index \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), is defined by
\[
m_b := \max\left\{
\left\lfloor \frac{(b+1)n}{4} \right\rfloor
-
\left\lfloor \frac{bn}{4} \right\rfloor,
0
\right\}.
\]

synth_4.title: Dyadic pilot resolution rule
synth_4.body:
The pilot resolution \(K_0(n)\), for sample size \(n\in\mathbb N\), is defined by
\[
K_0(n)=
\begin{cases}
1, & n<n_0,\\[2pt]
2^{\left\lfloor \frac45\,\frac{\log m_0}{\log 2}\right\rfloor},
& n\ge n_0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(n_0\) is the threshold for using the cubic estimator and \(m_0\) is the size of block \(0\) at sample size \(n\).

synth_5.title: Quadratic correction resolution
synth_5.body:
The quadratic resolution \(K_2(n)\), for \(n\in\mathbb N\), is defined by
\[
K_2(n)=
\begin{cases}
1, & n<n_0,\\[2pt]
2^{\left\lfloor \frac{4}{3}\,\frac{\log m_0}{\log 2}\right\rfloor},
& n\ge n_0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(n_0\) is the threshold and \(m_0\) is the size of block \(0\) at sample size \(n\). The floor is taken in the nonnegative integers, with value \(0\) when its argument is negative.

synth_6.title: Cubic correction resolution
synth_6.body:
The cubic resolution \(K_3(n)\), for \(n\in\mathbb N\), is defined by
\[
K_3(n)=
\begin{cases}
1, & n<n_0,\\[2pt]
2^{\left\lfloor \dfrac{\log m_0}{\log 2}\right\rfloor}, & n\ge n_0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(n_0\) is the threshold for using the cubic estimator and \(m_0\) is the size of block \(0\) at sample size \(n\). The floor is taken in the nonnegative integers, with value \(0\) when its argument is negative; the logarithm at \(0\) is assigned value \(0\).

synth_7.title: Blockwise marked histogram definition
synth_7.body:
The marked histogram \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)\), for coordinate \(i\), resolution \(K\), block \(b\), and evaluation point \(x\), is defined by
\[
H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,&n<256,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{K}{m_b}
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K-1}
\mathbf 1\{x\in E_{\ell,K}\}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in E_{\ell,K}\},
&n\ge256.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\mathcal S_n\), the sample of source records, and \(\mathcal T_n\), the sample of target covariates, each contain \(n\) records, and the parameters range over
\[
n,K\in\{0,1,\ldots\},\qquad
i\in\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\},\qquad
b\in\{0,\ldots,3\},\qquad
x\in\mathbb R.
\]
For \(K\ge1\), the cells \(E_{\ell,K}\) are
\[
E_{\ell,K}=
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K,(\ell+1)/K),&0\le\ell<K-1,\\
[\ell/K,1],&\ell=K-1.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(K=0\), the cell sum is empty and \(H_{i,0}^{(b)}(x)=0\).

Both samples use zero-based record indices \(r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), with an empty index set when \(n=0\). For sample channel \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\), the deterministic block \(\mathcal B_b^G\) and its size \(m_b\) are
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le r<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\},
\qquad
m_b=
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
-
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
The sample channel \(g(i)\) assigned to coordinate \(i\) is
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=0,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]
The covariate \(X_r^{g(i)}\) is the observed covariate of zero-based record \(r\) in that channel.

For zero-based source record \(r\), let \(Z_r\in\{0,1\}\) denote encouragement, \(D_r\in\{0,1\}\) treatment receipt, and \(Y_r\in\mathbb R\) the observed outcome. The observable marks \(W_{i,r}\) are
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\max\{0,\min\{1,Y_r\}\},\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\},
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}\mathbf 1\{D_r=1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The constant mark \(W_{0,r}\) accompanies zero-based target record \(r\); each remaining mark accompanies zero-based source record \(r\). In every block sum, the mark and covariate use the same record index.

synth_8.title: Clipped marked-density pilot vector
synth_8.body:
The pilot vector \(\widehat F(x)\), indexed by \(i\in\{0,\ldots,6\}\), is defined for real envelope parameters \(c_f,C_f\), a sample-size index \(n\in\mathbb N\), source and target samples \((\mathcal S_n,\mathcal T_n)\) each of size \(n\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\). For \(n<256\), set
\[
\widehat F(x)=\left(1,\frac12,\frac12,0,0,0,0\right).
\]
For \(n\ge256\), use \(K_0(n)\), the dyadic pilot resolution with exponent \(4/5\), and the block-\(0\) marked histogram \(H_{i,K_0(n)}^{(0)}(x)\) of \cref{obj:synth_7}, with the observable marks and zero-based record indexing of \cref{obj:synth_14}. Define \(\widehat F_i(x)\) by clipping this histogram value with the following lower and upper cutoffs, respectively:
\[
\begin{cases}
(c_f,C_f), & i=0,\\
(c_f/4,3C_f/4), & i\in\{1,2\},\\
(0,3C_f/4), & i\in\{3,4,5,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]

synth_9.title: Marked histogram residual
synth_9.body:
The residual \(R_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)\) is defined by
\[
R_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)
=
H_{i,K}^{(b)}(x)-\widehat F_i(x),
\]
where the marked histogram \(H_{i,K}^{(b)}\) and the clipped pilot vector \(\widehat F\) are defined in \cref{obj:synth_7,obj:synth_8}, respectively. The parameters are arbitrary nonnegative integers \(n\) and \(K\), data consisting of \(n\) source records and \(n\) target covariates, a coordinate index \(i\) among the seven coordinates, a block index \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), an evaluation point \(x\in\mathbb R\), and pilot-clipping parameters \(c_f,C_f\in\mathbb R\).

synth_10.title: Calibrated score acceptance set
synth_10.body:
The calibrated affine-score acceptance set \(\mathcal A_n\) is defined, for real inputs \(\alpha,c_f,C_f,L\), a sample size \(n\in\mathbb N\), and a pair of source and target samples each containing \(n\) records, by
\[
\mathcal A_n
=
\left\{
\theta\in[-1,1]:
\left|\widehat T_Y-\theta\widehat T_D\right|
\le
2\sqrt{\frac{2C_{\mathrm{mse}}}{\alpha}}\,
n^{-1/3}
\right\}.
\]
Here \(\widehat T_Y\) and \(\widehat T_D\) are the cubic estimators computed from the supplied samples with inputs \(c_f,C_f\), and \(C_{\mathrm{mse}}\) is the mean-square envelope evaluated at \(c_f,C_f,L\). Each cubic estimator equals zero when \(n<n_0\), the estimator threshold, and otherwise equals its pilot integral plus its linear, quadratic, and cubic corrections. The square root and negative power use their total real-valued conventions, including at zero.

synth_11.title: Known geometry calibration radius

synth_12.title: Tiled and coupled perturbations
synth_12.body:
The tiled perturbation \(u_{\lambda}\), for \(c_{\star}\in\mathbb R\), \(n\in\mathbb N\), and a cellwise sign vector \(\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{K_{\mathrm L}}\), is defined for every \(x\in\mathbb R\) by
\[
K_{\mathrm L}=\left\lceil n^{4/3}\right\rceil,
\qquad
h_n=c_{\star}K_{\mathrm L}^{-1/8},
\qquad
u_{\lambda}(x)=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{K_{\mathrm L}-1}
\begin{cases}
h_n\lambda_\ell\sin\!\bigl(2\pi(K_{\mathrm L}x-\ell)\bigr),
& x\in\operatorname{cell}(K_{\mathrm L},\ell),\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Each sign \(\lambda_\ell\) equals \(1\) when the supplied Boolean entry for cell \(\ell\) is true and \(-1\) when it is false. For \(0\leq\ell<K_{\mathrm L}\), the cells are
\[
\operatorname{cell}(K_{\mathrm L},\ell)=
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K_{\mathrm L},1],
& \ell+1=K_{\mathrm L},\\
[\ell/K_{\mathrm L},(\ell+1)/K_{\mathrm L}),
& \ell+1\ne K_{\mathrm L}.
\end{cases}
\]
At \(n=0\), the sum is empty and equals zero, with the convention \(0^{-1/8}=0\).
The coupled perturbation \(v_{\lambda,\tau}\), for any \(\tau\in\mathbb R\), is defined by
\[
v_{\lambda,\tau}(x)=\tau u_{\lambda}(x),
\qquad x\in\mathbb R.
\]

synth_13.title: Centered covariate witness direction
synth_13.body:
The witness direction \(g_{\dagger}\) is defined, for every \(x\in\mathbb R\), by
\[
g_{\dagger}(x)
=
\left|x-\frac12\right|^{1/8}
-
\int_0^1 \left|u-\frac12\right|^{1/8}\,du.
\]

synth_14.title: Coordinate marks \(W_{i,r}\) and sample blocks \(\mathcal B_b^G\)
synth_14.body:
The coordinate index set and coordinate ordering are
\[
\mathcal I=\{0,\ldots,6\},
\qquad
(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5,F_6)
=(t,q_0,q_1,r_{Y0},r_{Y1},r_{D0},r_{D1}).
\]
The sample channel of coordinate \(i\in\mathcal I\) is
\[
g(i)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm T,&i=0,\\
\mathrm S,&i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Vector, histogram, residual, and mark subscripts follow the correspondence
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}
i&0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ \hline
\text{coordinate}&t&q_0&q_1&r_{Y0}&r_{Y1}&r_{D0}&r_{D1}.
\end{array}
\]
For \(V=F\), \(V=H_K^{(b)}\), \(V=R_K^{(b)}\), or \(V=W_r\), the named-coordinate subscripts satisfy
\[
(V_t,V_{q_0},V_{q_1},V_{r_{Y0}},V_{r_{Y1}},V_{r_{D0}},V_{r_{D1}})
=(V_0,V_1,V_2,V_3,V_4,V_5,V_6).
\]

Index the source records and target covariate records from zero:
\[
O_r^{\mathrm S}=(X_r^{\mathrm S},Z_r,D_r,Y_r),
\qquad
X_r^{\mathrm T},
\qquad r=0,\ldots,n-1.
\]
Let \(Y_r^{\mathrm{clip}}\) denote the clipped observable outcome used in
\cref{obj:synth_7,obj:synth_8,obj:def:cubic-estimator}.
The observable coordinate marks, with this same clipping convention throughout, are
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{0,r}&=1,\\
W_{1,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\},
&
W_{2,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\},\\
W_{3,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}Y_r^{\mathrm{clip}},
&
W_{4,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}Y_r^{\mathrm{clip}},\\
W_{5,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=0\}D_r,
&
W_{6,r}&=\mathbf 1\{Z_r=1\}D_r.
\end{aligned}
\]
The mark \(W_{0,r}\) accompanies target record \(r\); the remaining marks accompany source record \(r\).

For \(G\in\{\mathrm S,\mathrm T\}\) and \(b\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), the blocks and their sizes are
\[
\mathcal B_b^G
=
\left\{
r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:
\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor
\le r<
\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
\right\},
\qquad
m_b=\left\lfloor\frac{(b+1)n}{4}\right\rfloor
-\left\lfloor\frac{bn}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
Their one-based counterparts are
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal B}_b^G
=\{r+1:r\in\mathcal B_b^G\}
=\{\lfloor bn/4\rfloor+1,\ldots,\lfloor(b+1)n/4\rfloor\}.
\]
One-based covariates and marks are defined together by
\[
\widetilde X_s^G=X_{s-1}^G,
\qquad
\widetilde W_{i,s}=W_{i,s-1},
\qquad s=1,\ldots,n.
\]
Thus, for a covariate set \(E\), the corresponding block sums satisfy
\[
\sum_{s\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_b^{g(i)}}
\widetilde W_{i,s}\,
\mathbf 1\{\widetilde X_s^{g(i)}\in E\}
=
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B_b^{g(i)}}
W_{i,r}\,\mathbf 1\{X_r^{g(i)}\in E\}.
\]
Block \(0\) supplies the training records, and blocks \(1,2,3\) supply the evaluation records. Each coordinate-\(i\) sum uses covariates and marks with the same record index in channel \(g(i)\).

synth_15.title: Baseline receipt–outcome cell laws
synth_15.body:
For a baseline compliance share \(b\in(0,1/4]\) and \(z\in\{0,1\}\), set
\[
r_z^{(b)}=\frac{1+(2z-1)b}{2}.
\]
Define the baseline conditional receipt–outcome probability mass function on \(\{0,1\}^2\) by
\[
R_z^{(b)}(d,y)=
\begin{cases}
r_z^{(b)}/2,&d=1,\\
(1-r_z^{(b)})/2,&d=0,
\end{cases}
\qquad z,d,y\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Equivalently, for each \(y\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
R_0^{(b)}(0,y)=R_1^{(b)}(1,y)=\frac{1+b}{4},
\qquad
R_0^{(b)}(1,y)=R_1^{(b)}(0,y)=\frac{1-b}{4}.
\]
Under this baseline law, receipt has probability \(r_z^{(b)}\) conditional on instrument value \(z\), and the binary outcome is independent of receipt with probability \(1/2\) for each outcome value. In the lower-mixture construction, the baseline share is \(b=\max\{a,n^{-1/3}\}\) for \(n\ge n_0=256\) and \(0<a\le1/4\).

synth_16.title: Tiled perturbation bump
synth_16.body:
Define \(\operatorname{bump}:\mathbb R\to[-1,1]\) by
\[
\operatorname{bump}(t)=
\begin{cases}
\sin(2\pi t),&t\in[0,1],\\
0,&t\notin[0,1].
\end{cases}
\]
Its restriction to \([0,1]\) is the function \(B(t)=\sin(2\pi t)\) used in the tiled perturbation. Its support is \([0,1]\), and its normalization is
\[
\|\operatorname{bump}\|_\infty=1,\qquad
\int_0^1\operatorname{bump}(t)\,dt=0,\qquad
\int_0^1\operatorname{bump}(t)^2\,dt=\frac12.
\]
It satisfies \(\operatorname{bump}(1-t)=-\operatorname{bump}(t)\) for \(t\in[0,1]\) and vanishes at both endpoints. The zero extension is continuous and globally Lipschitz with constant \(2\pi\); its restriction to \([0,1]\) is smooth. In particular, for \(\beta=1/8\),
\[
|\operatorname{bump}(s)-\operatorname{bump}(t)|
\le 2\pi |s-t|^\beta,\qquad s,t\in\mathbb R.
\]

synth_17.title: Distances between observed experiments
synth_17.body:
For probability measures \(P\) and \(Q\) on the same measurable observation space \((\Omega,\mathcal F)\), define the chi-square divergence by
\[
\chi^2(P,Q)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\int_\Omega
\left(\frac{dP}{dQ}-1\right)^2\,dQ,&P\ll Q,\\
+\infty,&P\not\ll Q.
\end{cases}
\]
The integral is understood in the extended nonnegative reals. Define total-variation distance with the probability-distance normalization by
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)
=\sup_{A\in\mathcal F}|P(A)-Q(A)|
=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left|\frac{dP}{d\nu}-\frac{dQ}{d\nu}\right|\,d\nu,
\qquad \nu=P+Q.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)\in[0,1]\). For the lower mixture, take \(P=M_\tau\) and \(Q=P_\star^{(n,n)}\) on the observation space of the independent source and target samples, each of size \(n\).

synth_18.title: Resolution-\(K\) interval cells
synth_18.body:
For a positive integer \(K\) and an index \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), define
\[
\operatorname{cell}(K,\ell)=
\begin{cases}
[\ell/K,(\ell+1)/K),&0\le\ell<K-1,\\
[(K-1)/K,1],&\ell=K-1.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus each cell includes its left endpoint, and the final cell also includes the endpoint \(1\).

synth_19.title: Target-density coordinate
synth_19.body:
In the marked-density vector, \(t\) denotes the target covariate density:
\[
t:=f_{\mathrm T},\qquad t(x)=f_{\mathrm T}(x),\quad x\in[0,1].
\]
Thus \(F_0=t=f_{\mathrm T}\), and the named-coordinate subscript \(t\) denotes coordinate \(0\): \(V_t:=V_0\) for \(V=F\), \(V=H_K^{(b)}\), \(V=R_K^{(b)}\), or \(V=W_r\). In particular, \(F_t=f_{\mathrm T}\). In \(\operatorname{bump}(t)\) and \(\int_{\Theta}P(t\in C_n)\,dt\), \(t\) is instead a local real argument or integration variable, respectively.
